issue.title: dice issues affecting coldtrace review
issue.body:
Agent review pasted below - I can share the reproducer .c files if wanted.

# coldtrace / dice: gaps that can lead to wrong conclusions from a trace

Date: 2026-11-11

Reviewed: coldtrace upstream `main` at `0e12143` (2026-10-12) with its pinned dice `14f5d73`.
dice upstream `main` is 9 commits ahead (`6245593`, 2026-11-11); those commits add the dispatch generator and rename chains, and leave the code paths discussed here semantically unchanged, so every dice finding applies to both.

Question: where can the data that coldtrace logs make an analysis of memory-safety or concurrency bugs come out wrong, either by reporting a bug that is not there or by hiding one that is?

Method: full read of coldtrace `src/` and dice `src/mod/`, `src/dice/`, then a host build (x86-64, glibc, gcc 13, Release) and one small probe program per suspected gap.
Findings marked **reproduced** were observed in a trace from that build; findings marked **code** come from reading only.
The probes and their runner are in `docs/coldtrace-trace-gaps-probes/`.
The trace consumer ("freezer") is not public, so this review describes what the trace says, and where a statement depends on how a checker interprets it, that is said.

## Summary

The trace has no way to say "events are missing here".
There is no end-of-trace marker, no per-thread sequence number, no drop counter and no timestamp.
Every gap below is therefore silent: a truncated or partial trace is indistinguishable from a complete one.

| # | Gap | Effect on analysis | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Crash or kill loses every thread's current fragment | The events leading up to a memory-safety crash are never on disk | reproduced |
| 2 | Threads alive at exit are never flushed | Whole threads missing from a clean run | reproduced |
| 3 | A child process deletes the parent's trace; `fork` children overwrite it | Trace directory holds a mixture of processes | reproduced |
| 4 | Events inside blocking calls and signal handlers are dropped by the reentrancy guard; a non-local exit leaves the guard stuck | Missing allocs and frees, a thread that goes dark | reproduced |
| 5 | Failed `realloc` is logged as a free | False use-after-free and double free | reproduced |
| 6 | C++ vptr accesses and `memset` are not logged | Missed use-after-free and races | reproduced |
| 7 | Call stack is not restored on `longjmp` | Wrong stacks on every later event | reproduced |
| 8 | `COLDTRACE_MAX_FILES` keeps per-thread windows that do not line up in time | Frees without their allocations, false use-after-free | reproduced in part |
| 9 | Only pthread, semaphore and TSan-atomic synchronisation is visible | False races, or missed ones, depending on the checker | code, symbols checked |
| 10 | Plain accesses carry no cross-thread order | Use-after-free across threads is only decidable through 9 | code |

## 1. The trace is incomplete without saying so

### 1.1 A crash loses the tail of every thread (reproduced)

Since `446fe0c` (2026-09-02) each thread writes into an anonymous private buffer (`coldtrace src/writer.c:224`) that reaches disk only when it is full or when the thread is finalised.
Before that commit the buffer was a `MAP_SHARED` file mapping, which the kernel wrote out even when the process died.

Nothing flushes on a fatal signal, `abort`, `_exit` or a kill.
With the default 2 MiB fragment size, each thread loses up to 2 MiB of its most recent events, which is exactly the part that explains a crash.

Probe `crash.c` performs a use-after-free write and then dereferences a null pointer.
Result: exit status 139, `freezer_log_1_0.bin` and `freezer_log_2_0.bin` both 0 bytes.

This also applies to any process that normally ends by being killed rather than by returning from `main`, which is the usual life cycle of an application process on a mobile OS.

### 1.2 Threads still running at exit are not flushed (reproduced)

A thread's buffer is flushed on `EVENT_SELF_FINI` (`coldtrace src/subs_pthread.c:60`).
dice publishes that for the thread running the module destructor and for threads that have already exited and are found dead (`dice src/mod/self.c:648`, `:679`).
Threads that are still alive when the process exits, such as detached workers and thread pools, never get it.

Probe `live.c`: a worker performs 1000 writes and then sleeps while `main` returns.
Result: the worker's file is 0 bytes; the main thread's file is complete.

Two narrower variants:

- A thread joined immediately before exit can still look alive to `kill(tid, 0)` and is then skipped. Seen once in 7 runs of `sigjmp.c`.
- A thread that ends without passing through dice's trampoline (cancelled, or not created through the interposed `pthread_create`) is never retired, so it is never flushed. (code)

### 1.3 Child processes destroy or corrupt the trace (reproduced)

`LD_PRELOAD` and `COLDTRACE_PATH` are inherited.
A child that goes through `exec` runs coldtrace's initialiser, which deletes every `.bin` file in the directory unless `COLDTRACE_DISABLE_CLEANUP` is set (`coldtrace src/config.c:58`).

Probe `child.c`: after 321 fragments were written, `system("/bin/true")` left 0 fragment files.
The parent then kept writing later fragment numbers, so the directory ends up with the end of the run and no beginning.

A `fork` without `exec` is no better: the child keeps the parent's thread ids, fragment counter and unflushed buffer, and both processes write `freezer_log_<tid>_<n>.bin` with `O_TRUNC` (`coldtrace src/writer.c:158`).
Probe `forkt.c`: two processes that each filled three fragments left three files in total, and the surviving thread-1 stream contains the child's allocation followed by the parent's free.
The global allocation and atomic indices are duplicated between the two processes as well.

### 1.4 The reentrancy guard drops events by context (reproduced)

dice's self module forwards an event only if the thread is not already inside a handler or between the BEFORE and AFTER of an interposed call (`dice src/mod/self.c:514`, `:532`, `:551`).
That is what keeps libc-internal calls out of the trace, but it also means that whether an event is recorded depends on what the thread happened to be doing.

Probe `sig.c`: a signal handler that allocates one block and frees the previous one runs twice, once at top level and once while the thread is blocked in `sem_wait`.
The first run is logged.
From the second run neither the allocation nor the free is in the trace, so the later, correct `free` of that block appears as a free of memory that was never allocated, and the block freed in the handler appears leaked.

The same applies to any signal that arrives while the thread is in `pthread_cond_wait`, `pthread_mutex_lock`, `pthread_join`, `malloc`, `memcpy`, an atomic operation, or inside coldtrace itself.
Which signals are traced is therefore a matter of timing.

If control leaves an interposed call without returning through it, the guard counter is never decremented and the thread stops producing events for the rest of its life.
Probe `sigjmp.c`: a handler calls `siglongjmp` out of a blocked `sem_wait`.
Result: none of the main thread's later accesses, allocations or frees are recorded, and because `EVENT_SELF_FINI` is suppressed by the same guard, the main thread's file is 0 bytes even though the process exits normally (6 of 6 runs).
Thread cancellation inside a blocking call has the same effect. (code)

### 1.5 A writer error silences a thread permanently (code)

Any failure to open or write a fragment (disk full, file-descriptor limit, permissions) puts the thread's writer in a failed state that is never left (`coldtrace src/writer.c:78`).
A failed growth of the call-stack array does the same for the whole thread (`coldtrace src/thread.c:80`).
The only sign is one warning on stderr; other threads keep tracing.

Related: if `COLDTRACE_PATH` is unset, longer than about 105 characters, or cannot be created, writing is disabled for the whole run with a warning only (`coldtrace src/config.c:12`).

### 1.6 `COLDTRACE_MAX_FILES` keeps windows that do not line up (reproduced in part)

When the fragment counter wraps, each thread overwrites its own oldest fragments (`coldtrace src/writer.c:270`).
A busy thread then retains its last few milliseconds and an idle thread its last few minutes.
The README notes that chronology cannot be recovered after a wrap; the consequence for analysis is stronger than that.

Probe `wrap.c` with `COLDTRACE_MAX_FILES=2`: the idle thread's file still holds its early `free(p)`, while the main thread's retained fragments start in the middle of its work and contain neither the allocation of `p` nor the allocation of the buffer it is writing to.
If the allocator hands the same address out again after such a retained free and the new allocation falls in an overwritten fragment, every later access to it looks like a use-after-free.
That last step is an inference; the probe did not get the same address back from glibc.

## 2. Events that are recorded differently from what happened

### 2.1 Allocation results are not checked (reproduced)

coldtrace logs a `FREE` before every `realloc` and an `ALLOC` after it, without looking at the result (`coldtrace src/subs_malloc.c:35`, `:43`).
When `realloc` fails, the original block is still valid, but the trace says it was freed.

Probe `realloc.c`, as dumped:

```
0) Allocated 16B of memory @…4330 [0]
2) Freed memory @…4330 [1]                 <- realloc failed, block still valid
3) Allocated 4611686018427387904B @0 [2]
5) write access 1B @…4330                  <- valid write, reads as use-after-free
6) Freed memory @…4330 [3]                 <- valid free, reads as double free
```

The same missing check gives an `ALLOC` at address 0 for a failed `malloc`, `calloc` or `aligned_alloc`, a `FREE` at address 0 for `free(NULL)` and `realloc(NULL, n)`, and an `MMAP` at the truncated value of `MAP_FAILED` for a failed `mmap` (`coldtrace src/subs_mman.c:18`).
`munmap` is logged before the call whether or not it succeeds.

### 2.2 Other unchecked results (code)

- `THREAD_CREATE` is logged with `*thread` even when `pthread_create` failed, so the pointer is whatever was in the caller's variable (`coldtrace src/subs_pthread.c:78`).
- `THREAD_JOIN` is logged when `pthread_join` failed.
- `LOCK_RELEASE` is logged before `pthread_mutex_unlock` and stays in the trace when the unlock fails.
- A robust mutex acquired with `EOWNERDEAD` is not logged as acquired, because only a return value of 0 counts.
- `pthread_getattr_np` is not checked when a thread starts, so the stack bounds in `THREAD_START` can be uninitialised.

### 2.3 The call stack is not restored on `longjmp` (reproduced)

The stack in each entry is a shadow stack maintained from `__tsan_func_entry` and `__tsan_func_exit`.
Nothing intercepts `setjmp` and `longjmp`, which the real TSan runtime does for this reason.

Probe `ljmp.c`: after three jumps out of a recursion seven frames deep, a write in `main` is logged with a stack depth of 23 where the real depth is 2.
Every event after the first jump carries frames of functions that are no longer active, and the array grows without bound in a program that uses `longjmp` for error handling.
A pop on an empty stack is ignored, so the opposite imbalance is hidden too (`coldtrace src/thread.c:193`).

### 2.4 Semaphores are logged as mutexes (reproduced)

`sem_wait` is recorded as `LOCK_ACQUIRE` and `sem_post` as `LOCK_RELEASE` on the semaphore's address.
Probe `semt.c` uses a semaphore with a count of 2: both threads appear to hold the same lock at once (acquire `[3]`, acquire `[5]`, release `[6]`, release `[9]`), and the unsynchronised increment between them is, according to the trace, inside a critical section.
A checker that reasons with lock sets would call that access protected.
A semaphore posted by a thread other than the waiter shows up as the release of a lock the thread does not hold.

### 2.5 Thread boundaries (reproduced)

- The main thread has no `THREAD_START` entry, because coldtrace builds dice with `DICE_MAIN_START_DISABLE`. Its stack bounds are therefore never recorded.
- A thread keeps logging after its `THREAD_EXIT` entry: thread-local destructors and libc's own exit path run later. For every created thread in the probes, the `thread exit` entry is followed by two `Freed memory @0`. A checker that takes `THREAD_EXIT` as the last event of a thread, and draws the edge to the joiner from there, would treat the later events as unordered against the joiner.

### 2.6 The zero flag is read by the tracer (code)

For 8-byte reads coldtrace dereferences the address itself to set `ZERO_FLAG` (`coldtrace src/subs_tsan.c:34`, `:191`), before the entry is appended and before the program's own read.
If the address is invalid, the fault is raised inside coldtrace and the faulting access is never logged.
The value is also sampled without synchronisation, so it can differ from the value the program then reads.

## 3. Things that are never recorded

### 3.1 C++ vptr accesses (reproduced)

`__tsan_vptr_update` and `__tsan_vptr_read` are empty (`dice src/mod/tsan.c.in:81`, `:86`).
GCC emits the first for every vptr store in constructors and destructors; clang additionally emits the second for every vptr load.

Probes `vptr.cpp` (g++) and `clrt.cpp` (clang 20): the object's constructor is logged as one 4-byte write to its data member, with no write to the first 8 bytes.
With clang the virtual call produces no read of the object at all.

The first thing a virtual call on a freed object does is load the vptr, and the classic race between a destructor and a virtual call on another thread is a race on the vptr.
Both are invisible.

### 3.2 `memset` and everything else in libc (reproduced)

`memcpy` and `memmove` are interposed; `memset` is not exported by `libcoldtrace.so`, and `__tsan_memset` calls an internal `memset` that publishes nothing (`dice src/mod/tsan.c.in:147`).
Probe `mset.c`: `memset(p, 1, 64)` leaves no entry, while the following `memcpy` and `memmove` do.
With clang, which turns large zero-initialisations and `memset` calls into `__tsan_memset`, the 256-byte write in `clrt.cpp` is missing as well.

The real TSan runtime also checks the buffers passed to `read`, `write`, `recv`, `strlen`, `strcpy`, `memcmp` and many more.
None of that exists here, and no uninstrumented code (prebuilt libraries, assembly, JIT output) produces access events.
An access that the trace does not contain cannot be reported, so "no use-after-free found" only covers instrumented code.

### 3.3 Synchronisation other than pthread locks (code, symbols checked)

The exported interposers of `libcoldtrace.so` are the pthread mutex, rwlock, spinlock and condition-wait functions, `sem_*`, thread create, join and exit, and `__cxa_guard_*`.
Not visible:

- anything built directly on futexes, which includes Rust's `std::sync` primitives and `parking_lot`;
- `pthread_once`, `pthread_barrier_*`, C11 `mtx_*` where libc implements them without calling the public pthread symbols;
- `pthread_cond_signal` and `broadcast`: dice interposes them but coldtrace does not subscribe;
- every annotation interface: `__tsan_acquire`, `__tsan_release`, `__tsan_mutex_*`, `AnnotateHappensBefore` and `AnnotateHappensAfter` are empty stubs, so code that describes its custom synchronisation to TSan gets nothing recorded;
- ordering through pipes, sockets, eventfd, or thread exit and creation outside pthread.

Locks are identified by address only, with no create or destroy events for mutexes, so a mutex that is freed and reallocated at the same address is the same lock in the trace.

Depending on the checker, missing synchronisation gives false races (the protection is not seen) or, where unrelated events are ordered through a reused address, missed ones.

### 3.4 Allocations outside the interposed set (code)

Interposed: `malloc`, `calloc`, `realloc`, `free`, `posix_memalign`, `aligned_alloc`, `mmap`, `mmap64`, `munmap`.
Not interposed: `memalign`, `valloc`, `pvalloc`, `reallocarray`, `mremap`, `brk`, and any allocator linked into the program under its own symbol names.
With such an allocator the trace has no heap events at all, only the allocator's own `mmap` calls.

Allocations and frees made while the guard of 1.4 is active are dropped, which includes those libc makes inside an interposed call.
On glibc, `strdup` is captured (probe `mset.c`), since libc's internal calls go through the interposed symbol; whether that holds on another libc has to be checked there.

Lifetimes inside arenas, pools and garbage-collected heaps are invisible, and so are stack frames: there are no events for a frame going out of scope.

### 3.5 Atomics (code)

Atomic entries have no program counter and no stack, so a report involving an atomic access cannot be attributed to code.
The requested memory order is not recorded, and every operation is executed as `seq_cst` (`dice src/mod/tsan.c.in:207` onwards) while coldtrace holds one of 128 spinlocks chosen from the address in 64-byte granules (`coldtrace src/subs_tsan.c:66`).
The recorded order is consistent, but the program under trace is more strongly ordered than the real one, so bugs that need weak ordering or a particular interleaving of atomics are less likely to occur while tracing.
128-bit atomics are not implemented; a program using them fails at symbol lookup.

The `__tsan_read*_pc` and `__tsan_write*_pc` hooks publish a null payload, which coldtrace's subscriber dereferences (`dice src/mod/tsan.c.in:181`).
Current GCC and clang do not emit them.

### 3.6 Symbolisation data (code)

`/proc/self/maps` and the mapped files are copied once, when the first non-main thread starts, or at exit (`coldtrace src/procmaps.c:125`).
Libraries loaded later cannot be symbolised, and an address range that is unloaded and reused resolves to the wrong module.
A single-threaded program that crashes never gets the copy.
Lines are read into a 256-byte buffer, and a file is skipped when its path is a substring of one already copied (`coldtrace src/procmaps.c:22`, `:78`), so `libfoo.so` is skipped after `libfoo.so.1`.

### 3.7 Pointer width (code)

Pointers are stored in 48 bits.
Top-byte tags are dropped, which is harmless, but addresses above 48 bits alias.

## 4. Ordering

Only two kinds of entries carry a global order: allocation events (one counter) and synchronisation events (a second counter).
Plain reads and writes have none, and there are no timestamps.

The order of an access in one thread against a free in another is therefore known only if the recorded synchronisation events order them.
With the coverage limits of 3.3, a use-after-free across threads either cannot be decided or is decided from an incomplete picture.
The two counters are also not related to each other except through each thread's own sequence.

The parts that were checked and hold: a free takes its index before the real `free` and an allocation after the real `malloc`, so reuse of an address is ordered correctly; lock acquire and release indices fall inside the real critical section; create precedes start and exit precedes join; atomic entries are consistent with the executed order.

## 5. Relevance for Servo

- Rust needs `-Zsanitizer=thread` with an instrumented standard library to produce access and atomic events at all, and rustc links the TSan runtime statically by default, in which case the hooks never reach coldtrace.
- Rust locks are futex-based (3.3). With an uninstrumented standard library no synchronisation is recorded; with an instrumented one, only its atomic operations are.
- Servo runs with dozens of long-lived threads and, as an application, is normally killed rather than exited, so 1.1 and 1.2 apply to every run.
- A build that links jemalloc has no heap events (3.4).
- SpiderMonkey is C++ with virtual calls (3.1), its own allocator arenas and a garbage-collected heap (3.4), JIT code (3.2) and signal handlers (1.4).
- Multiprocess mode and any helper process hit 1.3.

## 6. Before trusting a trace

1. The process ended by returning from `main` or calling `exit`, with all threads joined; otherwise treat the tail of every thread as missing.
2. No fragment file is 0 bytes.
3. Every allocation index and every atomic index from 0 to the maximum appears exactly once across all threads. A hole means lost fragments, a duplicate means a second process. Events dropped by the guard (1.4) never take an index, so this check does not find them.
4. The traced process did not `fork` or spawn anything, or the children had `LD_PRELOAD` removed.
5. `COLDTRACE_MAX_FILES` was not set.
6. stderr has no `coldtrace:` warning.
7. Discard `ALLOC`, `FREE` and `MMAP` entries at address 0, and do not trust a `FREE` that is directly followed by an `ALLOC` at address 0 from the same call site.
8. Read "no finding" as "no finding in instrumented code that uses pthread synchronisation".

## 7. Suggested fixes, by value

1. Flush on fatal signals and at exit for all live threads, or return to a file-backed shared mapping for the current fragment.
2. Add an end marker and a per-thread sequence number, and write a drop record whenever the guard or a writer failure discards events.
3. Check results in the allocation, mapping and thread subscribers.
4. Make the trace directory per process (pid in the path), stop deleting in children, and reset state in a `fork` child.
5. Implement the vptr hooks and `__tsan_memset`, and export `memset`.
6. Intercept `setjmp` and `longjmp`, and reset the guard on non-local exit.
7. Record `pthread_once`, condition signals and the TSan annotation interface; give atomic and lock entries a program counter.
8. Refresh the maps copy on `dlopen`, or record mapping changes as events.

None of this has been reported upstream.

## Appendix: probes

Run from `docs/coldtrace-trace-gaps-probes/`:

```
CT_SRC=<coldtrace checkout> CT_BUILD=<its build dir> OUT=<scratch dir> PYTHON=<python with lz4> ./run.sh <name> [VAR=value ...]
```

| Probe | Shows | Extra settings |
|---|---|---|
| `basic.c` | no `THREAD_START` for main, events after `THREAD_EXIT` | |
| `crash.c` | 1.1 | |
| `live.c` | 1.2 | |
| `child.c` | 1.3, `exec` | `COLDTRACE_TRACE_SIZE=8192` |
| `forkt.c` | 1.3, `fork` | `COLDTRACE_TRACE_SIZE=65536` |
| `sig.c` | 1.4, dropped handler events | |
| `sigjmp.c` | 1.4, stuck guard | `SETTLE=1` isolates it from 1.2 |
| `wrap.c` | 1.6 | `COLDTRACE_TRACE_SIZE=4096 COLDTRACE_MAX_FILES=2` |
| `realloc.c` | 2.1 | |
| `ljmp.c` | 2.3 | |
| `semt.c` | 2.4 | |
| `vptr.cpp` | 3.1 with g++ | |
| `clrt.cpp` | 3.1 and 3.2 with clang | compile with `clang -fsanitize=thread -c`, link against `libtsano.so`, preload `libcoldtrace.so` |
| `mset.c` | 3.2, `strdup` captured | |

One hypothesis did not hold: a detached thread's libc-internal allocations did not produce frees without allocations on glibc.

issue.title: tests: add shared engine contract suite
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds a shared `mozjs` API contract suite. SpiderMonkey is the reference implementation: every case asserts SpiderMonkey behavior, and the same source also runs against the QuickJS shim to expose divergences.

The first slice has 10 cases across five capability areas:

| Area | Cases |
| --- | --- |
| Property | get missing, set then get, define readonly |
| Element | set then get, script view consistency |
| Call | return value, pending exception |
| Buffer | new/write, detach |
| Rooter | custom rooter trace on explicit GC |

Each run writes normalized JSONL observations. `tools/compare.py` treats SpiderMonkey as the baseline: a registered QuickJS divergence is printed as a **known QuickJS defect**; any unregistered difference fails the run. `just contract-sm`, `contract-qjs`, and `contract-diff` run and compare both engines.

## Engine policy

- A contract case must pass on SpiderMonkey.
- QuickJS is checked against the same expectations; a shim divergence is a QuickJS defect, not a reason to weaken the test or change the shim.
- `known-differences.toml` records each accepted defect by case and field, with an owner and reason. Entries are never silent skips.

## Validation on `ohos-main` (`cb51f8a94`)

- SpiderMonkey: 10/10 cases passed.
- Pinned upstream QuickJS shim (`ae9eb96`): 9/10 identical; `rooter.trace_on_gc` is a known defect (SpiderMonkey `true`, QuickJS `false`). The comparison prints it explicitly.
- Negative check: an unregistered difference returns exit code 1.
- `cargo test --locked -p engine_contract_tests --no-run`: passed.

No QuickJS repository change is required or included. The QuickJS divergence remains a shim defect to be addressed there.

AI-assisted: Yes (agent session; written and tested by the agent)

issue.title: script: Run GC after document finished loading

labels.name: S-awaiting-review
labels.description: There is new code that needs to be reviewed.

issue.body:
This runs the GC after the document finished loading (with a delay given by pref).
We achieve this by using a new OneTimerCallback that calls script_thread to use gc.

Additionally, firefox seems to do something similar https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/source/layout/base/nsDocumentViewer.cpp#994.

Testing: This was tested with GC and without GC and showed a roughly 8 MB difference in memory consumed on one website.
Fixes: https://github.com/servo/servo/issues/48283

comment.body:
> Additionally, firefox seems to do something similar https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/source/layout/base/nsDocumentViewer.cpp#994.

When linking to searchfox or other forges, try to use a permalink. I'm guessing you meant this line:

https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/b42441b06bc2b98160f12ee2dff262dd55583a9f/layout/base/nsDocumentViewer.cpp#L980-L983
I think this is wrong and always returns 0. I think if we use an fst::Map newtype we can do ` self.0.as_fst().as_inner().size_of(ops)`

I know I was the one that recommended this in the first place, but after some more thought I think this is a) wrong and b) we don't need it, since  I think the mallocsizeof implementation of bytes will already return 0 for non-heap allocations. (It's wrong because this can be sent over IPC, and then the flag could be wrong in the other process since after deserializing it will always be heap allocated.
Could this be a newtype over `fst::Map<ResourceBytes>`?
Let's add a Safety comment here. Something like "The resource directory on ohos is read-only, so it's safe to mmap the file, since the contents can't change.".

issue.title: Add some performance tests
Prebuilt llvm-19 depends on libxml2
issue.body:
While trying to update the servo CI image (to ubuntu 26.04), I encountered the following error:

```
160.3       /home/servo_ci/.cache/cargo-ohos/ohos-llvm/19.1.4-79830f/linux-x86_64/llvm/bin/ld.lld: error while loading shared libraries: libxml2.so.2: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
160.3       clang: error: unable to execute command: No such file or directory
```

It seems there is a dependency on `libxml2` (presumably of the llvm toolchain), which the newer llvm-21 toolchain (from the host ubuntu) does not have anymore, so it's not on the system for our llvm-19. 

Not quite clear what to do about it, we could add a setup command (already a PR for that), and check if the linker works and have a recommendation if it fails, but that again is more complexity...


Option worth considering recommended by AI tooling:

>  B — the real fix, upstream in openharmony-rs/ohos-llvm-toolchains. The repack already has RUNPATH=$ORIGIN/../lib, so dropping a libxml2.so.2 into llvm/lib/ makes the toolchain
  self-contained the way the SDK's own LLVM is. Better still, build lld with LLVM_ENABLE_LIBXML2=OFF — it's only used for COFF manifest handling, which is dead weight for OHOS
  targets. This would fix it for every consumer, not just this image.

I was anyway considering compiling clang from source, so perhaps just going to a from-source LLVM-21 build is fine?

comment.body: Issue is solved in the new prebuilt llvm-21, which we built ourselves in CI

issue.title: net: Fix temporary storage for disk cache

labels.name: S-awaiting-review
labels.description: There is new code that needs to be reviewed.

issue.body:
Previously there were two mistakes in setting temporary storage for the disk cache.
1. We did not take the temporary storage directory from tempfile and added a file there but in the parent directory.
2. The tempfile was cleaned up before we could open the database.
These two combined with a working disk cache but not a temporary one.

We fix this by correctly appending the file to the path and keeping the tempdir alive until the database is opened. Afterwards the OS will take care to clean it up after the database is closed.

Testing: Because the file is inaccessible directly after creation we had to resort to testing with print statements. But we confirmed that it is working now.

comment.body: I could imagine the test creating servo two times sequentially, and asserting that something is not in the disk-cache the second time around (since the cache was temporary).

review.body:
> Testing: Because the file is inaccessible directly after creation we had to resort to testing with print statements. But we confirmed that it is working now.

The testing line here should usually refer to automatic tests. Is it difficult to add an integration test?

issue.title: Experimental Crubit Integration
issue.body:
Background Context: I work on https://crubit.rs a C++/Rust interop tool and I'm trying to add CMake support for it. Crubit works by ingesting a `.rlib` file and generating a `.h` and `.rs` file that provide C++ bindings to the rust code within the `.rlib`. I would like to get Crubit working with CMake and I think Corrosion would make that much easier for the end user (and me as a CMake novice) given it already does a lot of the heavy lifting to integrate a Cargo project into a C++ project.

This PR introduces a new `corrosion_experimental_crubit($target_name)` function that toggles on Crubit for a library target in a crate. The intended workflow is to toggle on Crubit for your target and then call import_crate:

```
corrosion_experimental_crubit(rust_lib)
corrosion_import_crate(MANIFEST_PATH rust_lib/Cargo.toml)
```

Within Corrosion this flag modifies the behavior of `_corrosion_add_library_target`, `_add_cargo_build`, and `_generator_add_package_targets`. When Crubit is enabled for a target, `_generator_add_package_targets` will fetch Crubit, check if the cargo subcommand is installed, and install from the fetched sources if not. 

`_corrosion_add_library_target` checks if the target is a Crubit library and adds the generated header as a byproduct when it is. Because a Crubit target has the generated header, we specify the target_include_directories. It also adds a dependency on our support libraries, which are provided by the fetch in `_generator_add_package_targets`.

`_add_cargo_build` now toggles the command it runs based on if the target is a crubit library. When the target is not a Crubit lib, the normal flow executes and calls `cargo rustc`. When it is a Crubit library, we call `cargo cpp_api_from_rust` (the subcommand we installed earlier). Under the hood, this subcommand performs a `cargo build` and so takes a lot of the same flags as `cargo rustc` but in a sligtly different CLI.

I am a novice at CMake, so please advice on style/idiom stuff. I've tried to match the style corrosion uses, but there's definitely some of the generator expression stuff I am not understanding super well.

issue.title: [InstCombine] Fold select (not (select a, true, b)), true, b to select (not a), true, b

labels.name: llvm:instcombine
labels.description: Covers the InstCombine, InstSimplify and AggressiveInstCombine passes

issue.body:
`foldSelectOfBools` canonicalizes `!a && !b` to `not (select a, true, b)` and `!a || !b` to `not (select a, b, false)` via DeMorgan's laws, and right below folds the unnegated absorption patterns:
- `select (select a, true, b), true, b -> select a, true, b`
- `select (select a, b, false), b, false -> select a, b, false`

However, it misses the corresponding negated absorption patterns when the inner select has multiple uses:
- `select (not (select a, true, b)), true, b -> select (not a), true, b` (i.e. `!(a || b) || b -> !a || b`)
- `select (not (select a, b, false)), b, false -> select (not a), b, false` (i.e. `!(a && b) && b -> !a && b`)

Match the one-use `not` of the inner select and replace the outer select's condition with `not a`. The outer constant arm is matched with `m_Specific(One)` / `m_Specific(Zero)` to avoid introducing poison on vector constants with poison lanes.

Alive2 proof: https://alive2.llvm.org/ce/z/j6YyBB

issue.title: ci: fix native gem compilation on Ubuntu 26.04
issue.body:
Restore the site build on Ubuntu 26.04 by updating the pinned GSL binding to the upstream [Ruby/GSL 2.8 compatibility fix](https://github.com/SciRuby/rb-gsl/pull/76) and supplying the remaining C compatibility options for GSL and Liquid-C. Pin the runner to Ubuntu 26.04.

<details>
<summary>Compatibility notes and validation</summary>

- The updated GSL binding still has [unprototyped function declarations](https://github.com/SciRuby/rb-gsl/blob/22bbb646d918aa80ee9e6b154d2ccd6538fe0ed8/ext/gsl_native/include/rb_gsl_array.h#L149), which need pre-C23 semantics with GCC 15. Compile it in C17 mode.
- Pre-include `stdbool.h` so Ruby 3.2's headers compile in GSL's C17 mode and Liquid-C's C99 mode.
- Liquid-C 4.2 requires Liquid 5, while Jekyll 4 requires Liquid 4, so upgrading the published Liquid-C version cannot replace the header compatibility option.
- [Ubuntu 26.04 CI](https://github.com/ustclug/website/actions/runs/42959269575) passed after restoring the existing cache through `restore-keys`: dependency installation, Jekyll Doctor, and the production site build.

</details>

issue.title: feat(navigation): 统一桌面 Sidebar 与移动 TabBar 的导航层级
issue.body:
## 目标：跨端共用一套导航心智模型

桌面 Sidebar 的一级入口对应移动端底部 TabBar：命名、顺序、功能归属和选中状态一致。不要让用户在不同设备或不同入口重新理解另一套目录。二级导航也要有明确的跨端对应关系。

## 已确认的产品规则

- 一级目录及各 Tab 不再提供目录折叠/展开按钮；原有日程、课程、校园、活动等分组不能因历史折叠偏好隐藏。
- 进入页面后使用子 Sidebar，并能返回上一层。本地提供根 Sidebar 预览，无需刷新页面才能切换导航层级。
- 删除 AI 助手（MCP）旁的说明文案、日历等项目旁的说明 icon 和对应解释入口。数量提示保留数字即可。
- 管理区的页面层级也始终展开，继续遵循现有权限可见性。
- 核心不是只删几个按钮，而是降低层级理解成本、减少桌面/移动及各位置之间的不一致。

## 已确认的一级入口与归属

一级入口与移动底部 Tab 统一为 **工作台 / 日历 / 校园 / 活动**，顺序一致。课程订阅是工作台中的功能，不独立占据一级入口。

| 一级入口 | 功能归属 |
| --- | --- |
| 工作台 | 个人概览、作业、待办、考试、课程订阅，以及活动关注和通知 |
| 日历 | 个人日历；沿用现有登录、数据权限和日历来源规则 |
| 校园 | 公开教学班、课程、教师目录，以及校车、天气、新闻、教室、校园网站等公共资源 |
| 活动 | 公开活动、活动日历、主办单位及详情；个人活动关注与通知放在工作台 |

设置、我的上传及管理入口等从用户头像访问，不作为根 Sidebar 目录或底部一级 Tab。管理入口继续严格按权限可见。工具与集成说明保留可发现入口，但不占一级导航。

根 Sidebar 仅呈现当前层级；不直接展开下一层内容。例如校车的“路线图”不再内嵌于校车下方，进入校车后再显示其时刻表、路线图等同级页面。课程、新闻、活动及管理队列等类似目录使用相同的子 Sidebar 模型，不能只给少数页面特殊处理。子 Sidebar 返回上一层为本地导航预览，不刷新当前内容、不丢失未保存输入或修改 URL/history；选择真实目的地才执行正常路由导航。

保留既有深链接、查询参数、片段、匿名/登录/管理员可见性及 Demo 投影。既有 /workspace/uploads 等路径保留兼容，但入口属于头像菜单。公开目录中不混放个人课程订阅或活动关注/通知入口。

## 二级呈现方案

- 桌面的二级目的地由当前层平铺子 Sidebar 呈现；移动 Web 从顶部菜单打开同源的当前层平铺 Drawer，底部固定四个一级入口。本地返回或预览上级时 Drawer 保持打开，选择真实目的地后才关闭并导航。原生 App 在当前 Tab 内使用功能目录及详情返回路径，对应相同的功能归属。
- 从详情查看上级根 Sidebar 是本地导航状态：保留当前内容页，展示已经拥有的根目录预览；无需刷新或重新请求页面数据。选择目的地时才进行正常客户端路由导航。
- 页面详情使用其真实集合父级；资源详情与页面内锚点不挤进一级 Tab。当前层目录平铺展示，不再内嵌下一层子树；管理队列进入对应子 Sidebar 后平铺呈现，保留权限上下文。
- Web 同级路由导航由桌面 Sidebar 与移动 Drawer 共同承担，使用同一份目录和当前态；页面内锚点继续使用独立的页面目录。

## 验收

- 对应的桌面/移动一级入口具有相同的名称、顺序、功能归属和当前态；从首页、搜索或深链接进入同一功能时，归属不矛盾。
- 根导航 → 子导航 → 返回/预览上一级流程清楚可用，本地预览不刷新页面。
- 不再出现上述目录或管理层级的折叠按钮、隐形折叠动作和历史隐藏状态；说明入口移除后，数字提示仍正确。
- 保留权限、正常导航、键盘/触屏可用性，以及晚到数量更新后当前项仍可见的已有保证。
- 同步规范和回归测试，提供相同可见数据、语言和视口的原生对照；独立审查与当前提交 CI 通过后交付。

本规则更新此前 [PR #1520](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/pull/1520) 的相关折叠与说明交互。现有移动端基线见 `iOS/Views/Shared/ContentViewTab.swift`；跨端页面归属与二级呈现应一并核对。

## 交付证据

Web 的统一导航已通过 [PR #1596](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/pull/1596) 交付：完整 48 项检查通过，4,846 项单元测试通过，生产环境已核实运行合并提交 3c1fc2dcb604。当前层平铺 Sidebar、移动 Drawer 和本地返回预览共用目录，个人订阅与公开页面按上述规则分区。

iOS 的统一导航已通过 [PR #166](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/pull/166) 交付：合并提交 f50783cde541 的源码树与已验收版本完全一致。手机、平板各 426 项单元测试和原有 71 个 UI 用例全成功、零跳过，各 93/93 个原生场景齐全；四个截图任务与完整 44 张原图通过。App/Widget 的已签名测试包为 3.0.0 / 20261114.010238。

两端 PR 均保留经过独立实看的原始前后对照及验证链接。原生合并后的 [自动 TestFlight 流水线](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/43471125069) 单独继续跟踪；此处完成的是统一导航的实现、验证与合并。

issue.title: feat(navigation): align four Web primary destinations and flat scopes
issue.body:
Part of #1575.

Align Web primary navigation with the confirmed four destinations: 工作台 / 日历 / 校园 / 活动 (Workspace / Calendar / Campus / Activities). One definition supplies desktop navigation and the mobile bottom bar. Root items remain discoverable for anonymous/loading/error viewers without exposing private leaf destinations or counts; calendar uses the existing sign-in/loading behavior.

Add a public `/campus` landing using the existing FeatureDirectory for academic catalog and campus services. Keep course subscriptions and activity follows/notifications in workspace. Move uploads, settings and permission-gated administration entry points to the avatar menu, while keeping their own page scopes reachable. Public tools, documentation, legal/help and search remain discoverable.

Sidebar rendering shows exactly the current flat level, without recursive `.items` trees. Entered scopes cover workspace, bus/map, campus/catalog/details, news/sources, Young/views, settings and admin/queues. Local back/root preview changes only navigation state, supports real ancestors (for example bus → campus → root), preserves main/form DOM, route/hash/query/history and keeps mobile Drawer open. Real destinations navigate normally. Owner/locale/user/role/loading/Demo expiry changes retire old local state and late data; count-only updates do not reset it.

Acceptance includes anonymous/user/admin/Demo ownership, late owner and count responses, locale and keyboard behavior, mobile safe area/overlay, existing directory/search and legacy URL contracts. Capture matching current-main before and final after evidence for the necessary root, bus, workspace and avatar desktop/mobile states; run relevant types/specs/units and real native cases against one fresh final producer with the original client budgets and deadlines.

No database/static/importer or native SDK changes. Delivery is tracked in Draft PR #1596; follow-up regression fixes and final current-head validation remain in progress.

issue.title: feat(navigation): 在子 Sidebar 本地预览根导航
issue.body:
## 问题

当前 `AppSidebar` 在 `sectionSidebar` 上下文中把 Back 渲染为指向 `/` 的链接；点击会离开当前内容页，并关闭移动抽屉。用户需要在当前页面本地预览根 Sidebar，再恢复当前分区，只有选择真实目的地时才导航。

## 范围

在现有 `AppShell` / `AppSidebar` 模型中提供可复用的本地 root/section 切换，接入当前 admin、settings、young 的 metadata 上下文。保留当前根/分区分组内容、当前页及 ancestor 判定、角色可见性和 Demo 投影。admin 的根预览必须使用真实根 groups，而非复用 admin-only groups。

沿用已确认的目录常展开、数字提示简化规则；不重复实现展开/计数变更。一级导航四组还是五组、新页面归属仍由父任务待确认，本项不决定 primary mapping，也不替代父任务整体跨端验收。不把 settings/young 现有分组内容顺带改造成另一套导航架构。

## 验收

- 根/分区切换前后保持同一 document、URL、history entry/长度及 main DOM 节点；不刷新、不重新请求内容页，不改变当前内容状态。根预览仍显示真实当前页/ancestor，能本地恢复当前分区。
- 使用准确双语语义的原生按钮区分“预览根导航”和“返回当前分区”；Logo/真实目的地仍是正常链接。键盘可操作，切换后焦点落在当前可见导航中。
- mobile drawer 内本地切换保持打开，Escape 仍正常关闭；选择真实目的地仍正常客户端导航，并沿用抽屉关闭行为。
- route/search、locale、viewer身份/权限或 Demo owner 变化时复位临时预览；晚到响应、计数更新或异步焦点任务不能让退休 UI、权限、数据或焦点回流。保持现有角色与 Demo 访问边界。
- 常展开与纯数字提示新规则不回退；原有当前项可见性、菜单/焦点安全与正常导航保证保留。
- 同步更新已有 settings/admin/young 真实消费者，覆盖 desktop/mobile、local restore 和 owner 变更；不删除旧业务、角色、DB 或 effects 守卫。提供相同可见数据、语言和视口的原生前后对照，经独立审查及当前提交必要 CI 后交付。

issue.title: fix(ops): await completion of the fixed organizer inventory CLI
issue.body:
The original fixed read-only production inventory [run43351135377](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/actions/runs/43351135377), source `08ca2b94cf28152e29eee87f47816d3171940d97`, finished its [Read fixed aggregate inventory step](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/actions/runs/43351135377/job/131643305385) with SUCCESS, but produced neither a report nor finite success/error output. Upload then failed because the fixed report file was absent. Validate succeeded; Prisma migration was skipped. The SSL-mode warning establishes that the pg Client constructor was reached, not a TLS failure or the actual pending phase.

The CLI calls `void main()` at its owned entry. Installed/CI-pinned Bun1.3.13 and pg8.23.1 expose a concrete lifetime gap: pg's connection deadline timer is unreferenced, and an unowned asynchronous continuation can be abandoned with exit0. The actual original CLI regression, using child-local installed pg overrides for delayed connection rejection and delayed cleanup, reproduces exit0/no report; only changing the entry to `await main()` makes it wait for cleanup and return redacted `{stage:"connect",code:"08006"}` with exit1. No socket or database is contacted by this regression.

## Acceptance

- Await the owned CLI entry without changing SQL, workflow, roles, SSL verification, connection/query deadlines or output/privacy rules.
- Preserve the original production failure. The correction does not establish its underlying DNS/TLS/connect/cleanup cause and is **not production acceptance**.
- Keep the regression on the actual CLI boundary, including asynchronous cleanup completion and redacted failure; retain the original four scenarios, including both real local PostgreSQL cases.
- Independent review and normal exact-source CI before delivery. Any later production read-only inspection requires its own authorized execution; do not silently retry the original run.

Current candidate on ordinary branch `fix/young-inventory-cli-lifetime` passes all five scenarios with zero skips, tests TypeScript, targeted Biome and diff checks. It is not committed or published yet. The original red and subsequent green are preserved separately.

issue.title: fix(shell): 展开侧栏目录并精简相邻说明
issue.body:
当前 Sidebar 将首层组、目的地子树和数字旁说明都作为独立展开操作，历史本地折叠偏好还能隐藏入口。本叶落实已确认的展开与精简规则，保留当前目的地模型，不先决定新的跨端一级结构。

Part of #1575。此叶完成不代表 Task #1575 完成。

### 范围与行为

- 取消所有当前首层目录和目的地子树的局部折叠控制；已有子目的地常展开，包括管理区 moderation 的 comments/descriptions/homeworks/suspensions 四个队列。保持原 URL、权限、真实上下文和唯一当前项，不新增或猜测二级 Tab 交互。
- 历史 `life-ustc.sidebar.v1` 的 `groups/submenus=false` 不再隐藏内容。保留全局 `open` 偏好、移动 Menu、Drawer Close/焦点归还/导航后关闭，以及桌面整栏 Rail。整栏展开收起和目录局部折叠是不同操作。
- 移除全部七类相邻 Info/details/说明入口：MCP、Calendar、Homeworks、Todos、Exams、Section subscriptions、Activity notifications。MCP 仅保导航名称与目的地。
- 六类数字继续使用原 summary 字段与原计数范围，不改变算法：个人日历、未完成作业、未完成待办、考试、教学订阅及未读活动通知。只显示数字，保留其可访问的单位/原范围语义与 `data-shell-count-value`；链接本身仍有准确独立名称。保留正值显示、0/未知不显示、匿名不含私有数字的既有规则。
- 不删除功能目录中的功能说明、页面帮助或公共文案；不修改全局 Menu/Close/Rail。

### 实现与既有消费者

主要呈现位于 `AppSidebar.svelte`，模型位于 `shell/navigation.ts` 与 `shell/types.ts`；无需更换存储 key、清理用户 localStorage 或新建导航框架。

同步维护现有 `ui.shell-layout-2/3` 与 `ui.navigation-discovery`，保留单一当前链接、角色边界、移动 focus/scroll、教学订阅只显示 summary 而不复制私人课程子树等约束。

- `tests/e2e/utils/navigation-count.ts` 及其既有调用者（Demo calendar/exams、shell projection、workspace、activity subscriptions、navigation context、property-priority overview）：从旧 `summary`/带单位可见文本迁移为纯数字 Badge，继续验证可访问范围与精确 marker，不删除计数正负控。
- `shell-discovery.test.ts`：保真实独立数据、locale、账号、DB/IO 账本；改验无相邻说明控件、六数字正确、label/Badge 无重叠或裁剪、晚 bootstrap 到达后数字和当前项仍可见。
- `shell-navigation-continuity.test.ts`：历史 false 偏好不再隐藏目录，保 reload/locale/current-anchor/整栏 Rail/Drawer 行为。
- `demo/young-workspace.test.ts` 的晚响应 MutationObserver：将仅匹配 `summary[data-shell-count-value="25"]` 的即时检查迁为任何同 marker 元素；保 attributes oldValue、added/removed nodes 自身与后代的短暂私有数字检测，不只核稳定最终值。

### 验收与可见证据

1. EN 1280 与 ZH 390 的正常目录和管理目录均无局部折叠按钮，旧 false 偏好不能隐藏任何已有目的地；管理四队列常开。
2. 七类 Info/details 全部消失，六数字及原范围/可访问信息保持；0、未知和匿名无私有数字。晚到数据不泄漏旧 viewer 数字，不使当前项失去可见性。
3. 键盘/触屏导航、移动开关与 Close/焦点归还、桌面 Rail、浏览器历史和唯一当前项继续成立。
4. 复用真实 owned fixture，捕获 EN1280/ZH390 普通目录与 admin/users 的原生 before/after；每对保持相同可见数据、URL、角色、locale、viewport、legacy-false 偏好和 Drawer 打开状态。仅保必要原图，不新增验收目录或框架。
5. 当前源独立审查及最新实际主线组合验证通过；真实失败保留，不放宽 timeout/retry/隐私断言。

### 仍由父 Task 决定和完成

主导航五项或四项、移动 primary/secondary 呈现、本地根 Sidebar 预览与返回上层，以及其他跨端归属工作均不在本叶交付范围。不得通过关闭此叶关闭 #1575。

- The original DOM snapshot at the focus read has `[data-overview-sections] aria-busy=true`; the snapshot after the urgency read has `aria-busy=false`. Original frames show the focus Loading line present before the measurements and absent afterward.

These are accepted pending-state behavior and must stay intact. This is separate from #1583 Teacher response latency and from #1530 JWKS authentication failures.

1. Change only `tests/e2e/src/app/workspace/overview/presentation-contract.test.ts`. Wait for the actual overview sections `aria-busy=false` using the existing expectation deadline.
2. Read focus, urgency, upcoming, links and the related personal/directory rectangles in one synchronous browser `page.evaluate` call so assertions compare one layout snapshot.
3. Preserve both 1280/390 widths, real owned fixture, business/effects guards, positive/nonzero geometry and every strict below assertion. Do not replace `>` with `>=`, add margins, remove Loading, change global readiness helpers, or increase timeouts/retries.
4. Integrate latest accepted main normally into existing PR #1565; validate its actual dependency graph with necessary types/format checks, fresh app/Worker and all unchanged six budgets. Run the one affected geometry case and the two existing held-pending cases, with an authoritative three-case list. Reuse unchanged transport evidence rather than replaying its full suite.
5. Independent review and the new exact-head natural CI remain required. Preserve the original failed evidence and distinguish local targeted results from full CI.

No production behavior, schema, authentication, origin or timeout changes, and no new worktree or validation framework.

issue.title: test(subscription): investigate missing mobile role dialog
issue.body:
Part of #1155. Related to #1570 and the earlier retained-scenario audit #1293.

The original Svelte PR1570 Subscription browser job fails in `subscription.kind-web-editor-location` without evidence yet establishing the mechanism. Preserve this failure independently from successful local observations.

Observed failure:

- Head `f5db91a617efffaf635e33d89e6b571e76c2d047`, run [43291782991](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/actions/runs/43291782991), [Subscription job 131445561932](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/actions/runs/43291782991/job/131445561932): 179 browser cases passed, one failed.
- The first nine role-save PATCH requests returned 200, and the ZH1280, ZH390 and EN1280 groups completed their save, database, reopen and Escape checks.
- At EN390, the native role-trigger click completed with a visible/enabled/stable target. The following role-radio lookup never resolved; it waited approximately 13.6 seconds before the unchanged 30-second test deadline closed the page.
- Expanded original DOM snapshots show no dialog/overlay after the desktop Escape. A brief body pointer-events lock was already removed by the resize completion and remained absent before/after the failed click. A residual overlay intercepting the click is not established. Actual click propagation, a transient mount/removal, and state/effect timing remain unproven.
- Original domain artifact `13983257724` is preserved: 13,446,053 bytes, SHA256 `95780be30269d2bbc157487fdcfd9b0f530f96b9df054be85e5a137a221be7ea`, all 545 ZIP members passed CRC. Original logs, failed trace and native frames are retained locally under `/tmp/life1570-subscription-*`.

One authorized controlled observation ran the complete unchanged twelve-combination journey once on the same producer. It passed in 14.0 seconds (8.4-second case body); all 24 native trigger clicks were trusted and propagated, and all twelve saves/reopens completed. The EN390 dialog mounted normally. This did not reproduce or resolve the original CI failure and cannot replace its evidence. The temporary sensor was removed and the original test SHA/mode restored.

Next evidence should be local to this case: bounded capture/bubble pointer/click/Escape/focus records plus actual dialog/overlay mutations, preserving event target/path, connection/default-prevention, timing and viewport. Retain the buffer when the deadline closes the page; attach it on failure alongside the original trace. Do not patch event methods, mutate UI, add interactions/waits, extend deadlines, split the twelve combinations or replace business assertions with observer output.

Acceptance:

- Establish the missing-dialog mechanism with actual event/state evidence, then implement and independently review the necessary correction.
- Retain all twelve locale/width/kind combinations, real writes, database/readback/reopen/Escape checks and final effects under the original 30-second deadline and retry policy.
- Demonstrate the complete original case and current-head CI passing after the correction; report the original failure and controlled observations separately.
- Adding a sensor or obtaining another isolated pass alone does not close this issue. Do not close it through the dependency PR without satisfying these criteria.

Additional evidence milestone: PR #1570 head `537c052f634f0d3fe106cde2c7a5b2769f52dca0` includes the independently reviewed case-local sensor without changing its original business flow or deadline. The Svelte 5.57.3 / Sonner 1.2.3 combination passed 90 related unit tests and twelve complete browser cases, including the role case in 9.4 seconds. Its Node-side JSONL contains 751 records across EN/ZH documents (SHA256 `d7162a887b5df11fe4d8c3927b6bf7dc2208bec55fb6f94bcac1a8a998b17639`). The original missing-dialog CI failure remains unexplained; this observation is not a mechanism/fix and does not satisfy the closing criteria. The issue remains open while the new canonical CI collects evidence.

The current #1589 head `5673d7d09dad884f09bd173b35e99f91149bd3a1` reproduced the missing dialog in [CI 43344048072, Subscription job 131619987065](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/actions/runs/43344048072/job/131619987065): 179 browser passes, one failure. This time the first ZH390 TA editor failed. Its 195 retained sensor records show a trusted mobile-trigger pointerdown reaching capture and bubble, followed by focusin, without a subsequent pointerup/click through a related trigger/dialog path or a dialog mount. The current sensor does not observe mouseup or unrelated paths, so this does not prove that no pointerup/click was dispatched elsewhere. Original native frames show a visible layout change; scrolling direction, layout movement and causal focus behavior are not established. The original artifact is 7,052,164 bytes, SHA256 `0f84d93212b46a18330eced2f88a04c585c14d92017a33644ab8c1ba3d75f835`, with full ZIP CRC validation. Next observation is limited to pointer coordinates, hit target, trigger geometry and scroll position during the immediate real gesture, preserving the complete business flow and 30-second deadline. No correction or acceptance is claimed.

One controlled observation of the complete original case with the bounded 250ms pointer-window sensor passed in 9.4 seconds (retry 0, original 30-second deadline): all twelve combinations and 24 trusted role-trigger clicks completed. In this run the ZH390 down/up/mouseup/click shared the same trigger, its rectangle and scroll position stayed stable, and no scroll event occurred in any bounded window. This did not reproduce the CI failure. Geometry reads may affect timing; no product correction or root cause is established. issue.title: feat(navigation): 在子 Sidebar 本地预览根导航
issue.body:
## 问题

当前 `AppSidebar` 在 `sectionSidebar` 上下文中把 Back 渲染为指向 `/` 的链接；点击会离开当前内容页，并关闭移动抽屉。用户需要在当前页面本地预览根 Sidebar，再恢复当前分区，只有选择真实目的地时才导航。

## 范围

在现有 `AppShell` / `AppSidebar` 模型中提供可复用的本地 root/section 切换，接入当前 admin、settings、young 的 metadata 上下文。保留当前根/分区分组内容、当前页及 ancestor 判定、角色可见性和 Demo 投影。admin 的根预览必须使用真实根 groups，而非复用 admin-only groups。

沿用已确认的目录常展开、数字提示简化规则；不重复实现展开/计数变更。一级导航四组还是五组、新页面归属仍由父任务待确认，本项不决定 primary mapping，也不替代父任务整体跨端验收。不把 settings/young 现有分组内容顺带改造成另一套导航架构。

## 验收

- 根/分区切换前后保持同一 document、URL、history entry/长度及 main DOM 节点；不刷新、不重新请求内容页，不改变当前内容状态。根预览仍显示真实当前页/ancestor，能本地恢复当前分区。
- 使用准确双语语义的原生按钮区分“预览根导航”和“返回当前分区”；Logo/真实目的地仍是正常链接。键盘可操作，切换后焦点落在当前可见导航中。
- mobile drawer 内本地切换保持打开，Escape 仍正常关闭；选择真实目的地仍正常客户端导航，并沿用抽屉关闭行为。
- route/search、locale、viewer身份/权限或 Demo owner 变化时复位临时预览；晚到响应、计数更新或异步焦点任务不能让退休 UI、权限、数据或焦点回流。保持现有角色与 Demo 访问边界。
- 常展开与纯数字提示新规则不回退；原有当前项可见性、菜单/焦点安全与正常导航保证保留。
- 同步更新已有 settings/admin/young 真实消费者，覆盖 desktop/mobile、local restore 和 owner 变更；不删除旧业务、角色、DB 或 effects 守卫。提供相同可见数据、语言和视口的原生前后对照，经独立审查及当前提交必要 CI 后交付。

issue.title: test(teacher): diagnose delayed detail response completion in browser acceptance
issue.body:
Part of #1155. Found while accepting #1579; the table change remains unmerged.

The original current-head CI run [43279624415](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/actions/runs/43279624415), Teacher job 131398666104, failed `ui.catalog-table-column-alignment Teacher` at `page-ready.ts:91`: visible skeletons remained 13 after the existing 10-second guard. Other 62 Teacher browser cases passed.

The retained native trace shows the teacher list completed, then `/catalog/teachers/1` rendered its teaching table. The detail shell-bootstrap returned headers in 9.854 ms but finished its body after 12,083.058 ms; the comments GET took 12,304.307 ms. Sidebar/viewer/description/comment loading remained in the original screenshot. All seven Worker probe requests eventually returned 200, with no recorded background errors. Neither that final success nor the visible table establishes timely page readiness.

Read-only independent review found no GET fixture hold, deferred route continuation, or prior-document bootstrap left pending. Cleanup starts after the assertion failure. The exact cause of the HTTP/body delay is unresolved; it is not established as CPU, database, proxy, or table-layout failure.

A single local diagnostic retained the original case, auth/origin, checks and timeouts, adding only browser event times and raw owned-socket byte/queue observations. It completed in 1.9 seconds (7.4 seconds including setup), with detail bootstrap 126 ms and comments 101 ms; the delay did not reproduce. Temporary observations were removed and both source files restored byte-for-byte. This diagnostic does not override the failed CI gate or prove a fix.

Acceptance:
- Identify the slow boundary using actual request/body timing; if necessary distinguish Worker response EOF/runtime cleanup from raw socket delivery and browser consumption.
- Apply an evidence-supported correction and retain native reproduction/regression coverage.
- Preserve original URLs, real auth, effects/lifecycle ownership and existing timeout/readiness guards; no retries or guard relaxation to obtain a pass.
- Validate the affected original case and current-head CI before claiming resolution.

The original Teacher artifact remains attached to the run (artifact 13974020443, SHA256 `cc80133388dd5f2a5b68e958d641a1348b2c9da0d702c951920c67f9d39f6388`); full ZIP CRC and digest were verified.


### Bounded runtime source review

The original browser trace shows both shell-bootstrap requests had no authentication signal and returned the anonymous `{viewer:null,navigation:null}` payload. Under the reviewed source, `hooks.server.ts` skips session resolution without that signal, and the shell-bootstrap handler returns before navigation/database reads. The HTTP feature inventory does not assign this internal route a persisted feature operation. These facts narrow the ordinary anonymous path; they do **not** measure the original invocation's cleanup/task counts.

A bounded source audit found runtime-cleanup registrations only in the app, auth and maintenance Prisma modules. Each runtime scope creates its own cache/resource/task sets; nested scopes inherit scheduling/environment capabilities, not another scope's resource collection. The registered callbacks directly disconnect their own clients. PrismaPg disposal ends its owned pool, which can wait for checked-out clients; no reachable self-wait cycle or cross-request shared pool was established for this anonymous bootstrap path.

No runtime change is justified by the current evidence. Always scheduling cleanup would alter existing no-background-task EOF/cancellation/error propagation, rather than being a semantics-neutral optimization. Cloudflare also bounds HTTP `waitUntil` work after response completion/disconnection to a shared 30-second window; it does not guarantee indefinite resource disposal. A synthetic held-cleanup unit would demonstrate the existing EOF policy, not identify this CI delay.

If the delay recurs, the specific missing boundary is the underlying response reader's `done` time versus cleanup start/completion and finite cleanup/task counts, correlated with the owned target/source socket's last-byte times. Header duration alone cannot distinguish these phases. Do not add broad browser logging, weaken readiness/ownership checks, or attribute the original delay to CPU, proxy, database or cleanup without that evidence. The unchanged local diagnostic pass remains a non-reproduction, not permission to disregard the original failure.

Source basis: [runtime EOF/cleanup](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/blob/1281cb4afcb928479fd7fdd9843c6ec9beb62a93/src/lib/adapters/cloudflare-runtime.ts#L228), [anonymous bootstrap branch](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/blob/1281cb4afcb928479fd7fdd9843c6ec9beb62a93/src/routes/_internal/shell-bootstrap/%2Bserver.ts#L24), and [Cloudflare waitUntil lifecycle](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/context/#waituntil).


### Original request completion boundary

The retained HAR distinguishes two delays: detail shell-bootstrap waited **9.854 ms for headers**, then **12,073.204 ms receiving** its complete 33-byte anonymous JSON; comments waited **12,261.193 ms for headers**, then received its 871-byte JSON in **43.114 ms**. Both ultimately returned 200 without recorded network failure. This is not evidence that both stalled during body reading, nor that a client timeout occurred.

On the original monotonic timeline, the skeleton assertion ran 146915.125–156916.914 ms. Bootstrap completed at 158924.519 ms and comments at 159335.985 ms; After Hooks began at 160336.210 ms. Both therefore finished after the readiness failure but before fixture teardown. The preceding list-page bootstrap finished at 145907.384 ms, before detail navigation at 146008.106 ms. Neither teardown-driven completion nor an unfinished prior-page bootstrap explains these timings.

The chunked bootstrap response and the client's awaited `response.json()` make response completion relevant, but HAR does not timestamp individual payload chunks, underlying reader `done`, cleanup/task counts, or owned-socket last bytes. Runtime cleanup can delay downstream EOF under the existing policy; these records do not establish that it did so here. Comments' separate pre-header delay also remains unexplained. No production fix, timeout change or retry is justified by this evidence alone.

### One original-source runtime-phase observation — 2026-11-13 UTC

One controlled execution used original Teacher source `3216dccd` (tree `cb4c06d0`), the unchanged complete case, canonical auth/origin and original 30-second test / 10-second readiness guards. A temporary, explicitly enabled observer recorded only raw pathname/layer/depth, finite task/cleanup counts and response phases. The case passed once (2.0 seconds; 7.8 seconds including setup); the original CI delay did not reproduce. This is **not a fix, exclusion of the original failure, or permission to close this issue**.

The retained raw log has 42 records: three requests, each paired by request ID across Worker depth 0 and nested-runtime depth 1. Both shell-bootstrap requests had zero registered cleanups and tasks in both scopes. Comments had one cleanup only in its nested scope and zero tasks. All six scopes recorded response return, first chunk, reader done, inline finish, cleanup begin/settled and downstream-close markers, within 1–2 ms after response return; no observed stream error/cancel occurred. The close marker is emitted **before** `controller.close()` and is not an owned-socket EOF measurement. These invocation-local counts do not prove the original CI invocation had the same resource counts.

The original trace ZIP is 1,971,029 bytes, SHA256 `58c9f2ab0e6acf433ca28172567a392dace47468f4cd55ebbfe0326d3ebf53cc`, with every member CRC verified. Raw Worker log is 14,981 bytes, SHA256 `cef89d3aa7437c3aaf0e9c9cc967a2340ddd23e7615c7e656767a51ecbdd08bb`. The first CLI selection attempt selected zero tests and never executed Teacher; it is not a business-test failure. All original CI failure evidence and prior boundaries above remain retained.

After all owned processes terminated, exactly the three temporary source paths were restored. The checkout returned clean to `5857f5b`, all refs/four stashes and 24 protected PNG bytes/modes were unchanged, and frozen install plus prepare restored its actual Svelte 5.57.3 / Sonner 1.2.3 / Lucide 1.70.0 / Socks 2.8.10 dependency graph. No host/auth/source fix, commit, push, CI retry or cancellation was performed. Mechanism identification and evidence-supported correction remain outstanding; keep OPEN.

issue.title: test(weather): cover unavailable and null-current consumers
issue.body:
Weather validation needs to distinguish two real states across consumers: an absent cache whose real upstream attempt fails, and a fresh cached snapshot whose current temperature is null. A null current reading is a valid snapshot, not an unavailable endpoint; missing optional data must not create fabricated metrics or forecasts.

Acceptance:

- Real isolated Worker REST, GraphQL and public native MCP consumers distinguish unavailable from null-current snapshots, with the existing anonymous/public policy and a separate actual Bearer/JWKS/grant case. Do not substitute a fake principal or bypass authentication.
- Exact owned upstream failure responses are actually matched; reject unexpected provider-origin requests. Preserve the original request URLs, statuses, deadlines and source freshness behavior.
- English desktop and Chinese mobile weather pages show the expected temperature/unknown/unavailable states, omit absent optional metrics and empty forecast sections, and retain independently checked update time and provider attribution.
- Consumer reads preserve the exact arranged cache/history and every business table. The expected real REST 503 may produce only its precisely asserted request/edge runtime observations and corresponding metric counters; prove exact event/status/request-ID association, bounded timestamps and counter increments instead of excluding whole observability tables. Keep the existing positive populated-snapshot cases.
- Preserve KV/provider fault distinctions in unit/route coverage; test an upstream-unavailable response separately from a storage exception. Do not claim a real Worker KV fault was injected if only its unit boundary was tested.
- Use Playwright's documented array-option tuple syntax so both owned provider responses reach the fixture. Preserve the original failing runs and the matched/rejected diagnostic that established the discarded second response.

Part of #1155. The related existing Room array-fixture defect is tracked independently in #1580. This delivery extends validation; it does not change production weather or authentication behavior.

issue.title: fix(test): preserve all outbound JSON fixture responses
issue.body:
Playwright treats a two-object array used directly as a fixture value as `[value, options]`. The current outbound-response fixture accepts either one response or an array, but several Room consumers pass two response objects without the required outer tuple. Only `room_maps.json` reaches the child Worker; `building_img_rules.json` is interpreted as fixture options and is lost.

The installed Playwright implementation confirms this (`isFixtureTuple` checks whether the second array entry is an object, then takes the first entry as the fixture value). The [official array-option documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-fixtures#array-as-an-option-value) requires `[actualArray, { scope: 'test' }]`.

Confirmed existing callers:

- `tests/e2e/src/app/demo/rooms.test.ts`: two-response `test.use`.
- `tests/integration/rest/demo/rooms.test.ts`: two-response `test.use`.
- `tests/e2e/src/app/rooms/navigation.test.ts`: two-response `ownedTest.extend` for raw-code normalization.

The Weather WIP independently exposed this exact problem: its strict origin guard rejected the high-campus request even though the URL exactly matched the second declared response. Its diagnostic recorded no matches and that rejected URL. This does not establish that all older Room cases used the second endpoint; however, previous green results cannot prove that the second declared response was controlled, because unmatched requests retain the default transport.

Deliverable:

- Wrap all existing array-valued outbound-response fixtures correctly, preserving response payloads, normal scope and every business assertion.

issue.title: test(weather): cover unavailable and null-current consumers
issue.body:
Weather validation needs to distinguish two real states across consumers: an absent cache whose real upstream attempt fails, and a fresh cached snapshot whose current temperature is null. A null current reading is a valid snapshot, not an unavailable endpoint; missing optional data must not create fabricated metrics or forecasts.

Acceptance:

- Real isolated Worker REST, GraphQL and public native MCP consumers distinguish unavailable from null-current snapshots, with the existing anonymous/public policy and a separate actual Bearer/JWKS/grant case. Do not substitute a fake principal or bypass authentication.
- Exact owned upstream failure responses are actually matched; reject unexpected provider-origin requests. Preserve the original request URLs, statuses, deadlines and source freshness behavior.
- English desktop and Chinese mobile weather pages show the expected temperature/unknown/unavailable states, omit absent optional metrics and empty forecast sections, and retain independently checked update time and provider attribution.
- Consumer reads preserve the exact arranged cache/history and every business table. The expected real REST 503 may produce only its precisely asserted request/edge runtime observations and corresponding metric counters; prove exact event/status/request-ID association, bounded timestamps and counter increments instead of excluding whole observability tables. Keep the existing positive populated-snapshot cases.
- Preserve KV/provider fault distinctions in unit/route coverage; test an upstream-unavailable response separately from a storage exception. Do not claim a real Worker KV fault was injected if only its unit boundary was tested.
- Use Playwright's documented array-option tuple syntax so both owned provider responses reach the fixture. Preserve the original failing runs and the matched/rejected diagnostic that established the discarded second response.

Part of #1155. The related existing Room array-fixture defect is tracked independently in #1580. This delivery extends validation; it does not change production weather or authentication behavior.

issue.title: fix(test): preserve all outbound JSON fixture responses
issue.body:
Playwright treats a two-object array used directly as a fixture value as `[value, options]`. The current outbound-response fixture accepts either one response or an array, but several Room consumers pass two response objects without the required outer tuple. Only `room_maps.json` reaches the child Worker; `building_img_rules.json` is interpreted as fixture options and is lost.

The installed Playwright implementation confirms this (`isFixtureTuple` checks whether the second array entry is an object, then takes the first entry as the fixture value). The [official array-option documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-fixtures#array-as-an-option-value) requires `[actualArray, { scope: 'test' }]`.

Confirmed existing callers:

- `tests/e2e/src/app/demo/rooms.test.ts`: two-response `test.use`.
- `tests/integration/rest/demo/rooms.test.ts`: two-response `test.use`.
- `tests/e2e/src/app/rooms/navigation.test.ts`: two-response `ownedTest.extend` for raw-code normalization.

The Weather WIP independently exposed this exact problem: its strict origin guard rejected the high-campus request even though the URL exactly matched the second declared response. Its diagnostic recorded no matches and that rejected URL. This does not establish that all older Room cases used the second endpoint; however, previous green results cannot prove that the second declared response was controlled, because unmatched requests retain the default transport.
