issue.title: fix(young): migrate organizer membership without expanding existing follows
issue.body:
Young activities can have multiple organizers, but the current importer normalizes the whole comma-separated display label into one `YoungOrganizer`. This loses individual organizer membership and gives filtering, counts and follows the wrong identity model.

A read-only sample of the live API’s first page contains 20 activities, including five with multiple upstream organizer IDs and a combined display label. For example, `850a10dcbada580177b6b3cde6368de2` has two upstream IDs and the label `芳草社图书馆志愿服务分队,学生科乐喜剧社`, but only one local `organizerId`. This is a bounded sample, not a full inventory or proof that ID/name positions always correspond.

Current contract and confirmed keys:

- `prisma/schema.prisma:1987–2080` and `prisma/migrations/20260901210000_add_young_events/migration.sql:2–27`: **YoungEvent.id is the integer primary key**; `youngId` is a separate unique public/source identifier. `YoungOrganizer.id` is a string primary key. Preserve both existing identity spaces.
- `src/static-loader/young-plan.ts:181–197` preserves `upstreamOrganizerIds[]` but reads the combined `organizer_dictText` as one string, falling back to `sponsor_dictText`. `import-young.ts:36–62,203–208` creates/links one entity using the normalized entire label. The original organizer migration also backfilled whole labels using deterministic MD5 IDs; later imports use CUIDs.
- `snapshot-values.ts:31–35` uses `String(value)`, which would implicitly join an array. No explicit organizer-array join was found in the inspected client-core/static/crawler source. Static’s JSON store instead places real arrays in child tables (`static/src/sqlite_store.py:675–690`), which the current Young parent-row mapper does not reconstruct. Verify the actual source representation rather than inventing a join location.
- `young-event-query.ts:112–113`, `young-table-filter-query.ts:66–77`, `young-calendar-query.ts:48–57` and `young-organizer-service.ts:41–46,132–151` all assume the scalar relationship. Web organizer multi-selection currently means OR within that field; REST retains a single organizer-ID filter.
- `young-notification-service.ts:96–123` creates per-organizer/day digests. Follows are unique by `(userId, organizerId)`; unsubscribing deletes that organizer’s unread notifications. Direct event subscriptions/reminders are a separate identity and must not be duplicated.

Proposed staged migration:

1. **Inventory and expand.** Read-only verify the target database’s actual constraints and drift before designing DDL. Add an explicit `YoungEventOrganizer` relationship using `eventId Int → YoungEvent.id` and `organizerId String → YoungOrganizer.id`, unique on the pair, with source order/provenance where needed. Add authoritative source-ID mapping and name aliases. Preserve original labels, `rawJson`, old scalar links, existing local IDs, subscriptions and notification history during rollout. Do not rewrite already-applied migrations.
2. **Resolve members without guessing.** Prefer authoritative upstream IDs/dictionaries. Do not blindly split normalized display names or zip deduplicated IDs with labels: names may contain commas; NFKC changes full-width commas; duplicate IDs, reordered labels, unequal cardinality, missing labels and sponsor fallback all need explicit handling. Retain unresolved mappings and provenance. Do not conflate sponsors with organizers. Keep verified single-organizer IDs stable; names and aliases must not silently merge distinct source identities.
3. **Idempotent dual-write/backfill.** Upsert atomic organizers and replace an event’s membership edges transactionally; preserve snapshot freshness/source-missing behavior. Keep a reversible old-to-new mapping ledger. Compare membership, counts and unmapped rows before switching readers; invalidate relevant catalog caches. Backfill alone must not emit `event_changed` or replay reminders—current `youngEventState` intentionally excludes organizer fields.
4. **Switch all readers together.** Add an explicit `organizers[]` DTO and update list/detail/filter/calendar/count/UI and generated-client contracts. Retain documented legacy fields and old organizer URLs during compatibility rollout; never pick an arbitrary first organizer as a replacement. Use membership `EXISTS`/distinct event identities so pagination, totals, unknown-date counts and calendars do not multiply rows. Preserve Web OR semantics and cross-field AND semantics. Update sealed Demo projections without falling through to real readers.
5. **Preserve follow intent and define digest deduplication before enabling migrated follows.** A follow of a legacy composite `A,B` cannot automatically become follows of A and B: that broadens “this combined organizer” into every activity from either member. Keep the legacy target semantics/ID until an explicit conversion policy exists. Preserve historical notification IDs, read state and dedupe keys. Within each digest, count each event once. For a user following both A and B, explicitly choose retained per-organizer grouping versus a new user/day union with event-ID deduplication; the latter is recommended for new atomic-follow delivery but requires recipient reasons and correct partial-unsubscribe behavior. Do not silently ship cross-organizer duplicate notifications or rewrite delivered history. Direct event reminder deduplication remains unchanged.
6. **Contract only after rollback validation.** Remove old columns/compatibility behavior only after readers and clients migrate and validation is complete. Reversibility depends on keeping old fields and the mapping ledger; dropping the join cannot undo expanded follows or already-delivered notifications.

Acceptance:

- Unit/import coverage for single/multiple/duplicate IDs, names containing commas, whitespace/NFKC variants, aliases/renames, missing or mismatched source pairs, sponsor fallback, ordering and repeated imports.
- Real database migration/backfill verification: stable IDs, no lost memberships, no unintended subscription fan-out, no synthetic event-change notifications, preserved read history and a tested rollback.
- REST/Web checks for membership filtering, OR/AND semantics, distinct pagination/count/calendar behavior, old IDs/URLs and the new DTO. Co-hosted activities followed through multiple organizers must satisfy the selected digest policy; unsubscribing one organizer must retain valid remaining reasons.
- Keep unresolved source-pairing and legacy-follow/digest policy decisions visible before implementation. This issue proposes the correction; no production migration or activation has been performed.

Follow-up: dictionary and safe backfill boundaries

- The inspected fetcher currently stores only Young enrolment/end-list payloads (`static/src/young.py:20–25,107–120,185–236`); its per-record model is opaque. No authoritative organizer-ID/name dictionary fetch or pairing contract was found in the bounded static/crawler/client-core source inspection. The existing department dictionary comes from the **different** `catalog.ustc.edu.cn/api/teach/department/college-tree` service (`static/src/utils/catalog.py:44–46,65–89`); matching-looking department codes are not proof of the Young identifier namespace. Do not use it as an organizer dictionary without evidence.
- A read-only metadata/schema check of the already-local snapshot (no download or event-table scan) found Young list/place tables but no organizer dictionary table. That local snapshot reports `young_events_mode=incremental`, with no accepted full-snapshot freshness marker, so it is not authority for the live data’s complete mapping. The live 20-row API sample has 15 one-ID and five multi-ID rows; even its one-ID rows are only candidates because the public projection hides whether the organizer label used sponsor fallback.
- Automatic name backfill is eligible only with raw provenance: one genuine organizer source ID paired with the actual non-fallback organizer label, or an authoritative dictionary mapping; conflicting observations/aliases need review. Matching the number of comma-separated IDs and names does not prove positional correspondence. Multi-ID names without confirmed pairing remain unresolved; do not fabricate names, silently zip, or switch their legacy follows. Schema expansion and shadow validation can proceed independently of resolving every row, but reader/follow cutover must respect the unresolved-coverage policy.
- **Explicit constraint transition:** `YoungOrganizer.normalizedName` is currently unique. Distinct authoritative source IDs with the same display name must not be merged through that constraint or the importer’s whole-name lookup. Introduce source-ID identity and an alias relation first, retain stable local IDs, and change writer lookup from normalized-name identity to source identity. Name lookup must return zero/one/multiple candidates explicitly. After all old writers are retired and collisions are inventoried, replace the normalized-name unique constraint with a non-unique lookup index; aliases may legitimately name multiple distinct organizers. Do not invent suffixed normalized names merely to satisfy the old constraint.
- Rolling back that uniqueness change is not automatically lossless once real same-name identities exist. Keep dual-write/legacy projections and the mapping ledger; refuse a rollback that would merge identities, delete valid rows or reintroduce a unique constraint over real collisions. A schema migration alone cannot reverse delivered notifications or expanded user intent.


## Verified upstream roles and resolver path

The [official public Young business bundle](https://young.ustc.edu.cn/login/sc-wisdom-group-learning/static/js/chunk-04730e1f.f833b409.js), SHA256 `6f80fb8904e7e699e40b46ec2d7fc7e70ddf96f2ca4026017b35ad6c99922253`, explicitly distinguishes `sponsor` (主办单位) from `organizer` (承办单位). Both selectors accept multiple IDs from the same tree, and submit each role’s ID array separately as CSV. This establishes multi-valued source roles; it does not prove positional correspondence with `*_dictText` or make joined names reversible. The existing organizer-first/sponsor-fallback projection is compatibility behavior, not evidence that the role mapping is correct. The migration must preserve the role dimension and review current API/UI wording and legacy-follow intent before changing that projection.

Its tree loader uses the [public app bundle](https://young.ustc.edu.cn/login/sc-wisdom-group-learning/static/js/app.6a3a219d.js) export `jb`, resolving to GET `/sysdepart/sysDepart/queryTreeList`. The consumer converts node titles to labels and uses the bundled tree selector’s ID values. This provides a concrete source-dictionary resolver to investigate; no dictionary API call, actual node retrieval, permission/tenant completeness check or pairing of stored IDs has yet been performed. The HTTP helper uses authenticated requests and its existing GET protocol, so a bare anonymous endpoint probe would not establish dictionary availability. No catalog-service namespace substitution is justified.

[PR #1590](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/pull/1590) delivered the first evidence-preservation stage: real snapshot string-array children survive into the existing raw JSON column without changing promoted scalar fields or follow semantics. Thirty-six related unit cases, one real SQLite integration case, test types and targeted formatting checks passed. The separately recorded first integration invocation failed before case execution; the normal runner subsequently passed with the existing verified local runtime environment. This repairs future accepted inputs only: historical backfill, role-correct membership, schema expansion and production cutover remain incomplete, so this issue stays open. All 38 current-head CI jobs and 47 checks passed before independent review and squash merge as `827d46d9c0abe4b70e7988db18e9e02ac2a619e9`; the canonical deployment reports that version. [PR #1591](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/pull/1591) adds unresolved event-local source observations without changing public readers or follows, and [PR #1592](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/pull/1592) adds the fixed read-only aggregate inventory operation. Both remain under validation; neither completes the membership migration or activates converted follows.

## Read-only inventory preparation

The inventory below has been independently reviewed and executed successfully against the existing **local development PostgreSQL 16.14 database**, using one READ ONLY / REPEATABLE READ transaction and ending in ROLLBACK. The five expected tables and key types were present. This validates local SQL syntax/types and execution, not production counts or comprehensive edge-case correctness. The first local metadata query exposed an internal-char concatenation ambiguity; explicit text casts corrected it before the successful run.

No production inventory, migration or follow conversion has run. A separately verified, complete read-only production connection is still required. The output contains only metadata fingerprints and aggregates; no user/source IDs, names, labels or notification contents are exported. Review the target endpoint/schema fingerprint before accepting results. Use fail-fast noninteractive `psql -X --set=ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --file inventory.sql` with the verified connection profile.

`row_security=off` intentionally fails if policies would filter rows, rather than accepting a restricted zero count; it does not grant a policy bypass or alter roles. See [PostgreSQL row-security semantics](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/runtime-config-client.html#GUC-ROW-SECURITY) and [read-only transactions](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/sql-set-transaction.html).

<details>
<summary>Read-only inventory SQL — review before running on the verified target</summary>

```sql
-- Inventory draft: locally validated on PostgreSQL 16.14 in READ ONLY / REPEATABLE READ, ending in ROLLBACK.
-- No production execution or migration readiness is claimed. No connection details belong here.
-- Review the target database fingerprint out of band before accepting results.
-- Intended runner: psql --no-psqlrc --set=ON_ERROR_STOP=on --file <this file>
-- On any error, stop and disconnect (aborts this transaction); do not retry with RLS enabled.
-- Read-only, one consistent snapshot, aggregate-only output; no DDL/temp tables/functions.
-- No organizer-name splitting, source-ID/name zipping, or inferred atomic identity.
BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY;
SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '30s';
SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '2s';
SET LOCAL idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = '60s';
SET LOCAL row_security = off;
SET LOCAL search_path = pg_catalog;

-- 1. Target/schema fingerprints, actual key types, and role/RLS completeness context.
-- row_security=off DOES NOT bypass RLS: a query subject to a policy must error.
WITH wanted(name) AS (VALUES
  ('YoungEvent'), ('YoungOrganizer'), ('UserYoungOrganizerSubscription'),
  ('UserYoungEventSubscription'), ('YoungNotification')
), relations AS (
  SELECT c.oid, c.relname, c.relrowsecurity, c.relforcerowsecurity,
         c.relowner = (SELECT oid FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user) AS owned_by_current_role
  FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
  JOIN wanted w ON w.name = c.relname WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relkind = 'r'
), column_shapes AS (
  SELECT r.relname, a.attname, format_type(a.atttypid, a.atttypmod) AS type,
         a.attnotnull, a.attidentity,
         coalesce(pg_get_expr(d.adbin, d.adrelid), '') AS default_expression
  FROM relations r JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = r.oid
  LEFT JOIN pg_attrdef d ON d.adrelid = a.attrelid AND d.adnum = a.attnum
  WHERE a.attnum > 0 AND NOT a.attisdropped
), fingerprints AS (
  SELECT
    (SELECT md5(string_agg(concat_ws('|',relname,attname,type,attnotnull,attidentity,default_expression), E'\n'
      ORDER BY relname COLLATE "C", attname COLLATE "C")) FROM column_shapes) AS columns,
    (SELECT md5(string_agg(r.relname || '|' || c.contype::text || '|' || pg_get_constraintdef(c.oid), E'\n'
      ORDER BY r.relname COLLATE "C", c.conname COLLATE "C"))
      FROM relations r JOIN pg_constraint c ON c.conrelid = r.oid) AS constraints,
    (SELECT md5(string_agg(r.relname || '|' || i.indisvalid::text || '|' || i.indisready::text || '|' || pg_get_indexdef(i.indexrelid), E'\n'
      ORDER BY r.relname COLLATE "C", pg_get_indexdef(i.indexrelid) COLLATE "C"))
      FROM relations r JOIN pg_index i ON i.indrelid = r.oid) AS indexes,
    (SELECT md5(coalesce(string_agg(r.relname || '|' || p.polname || '|' || p.polcmd::text || '|' || p.polroles::text || '|' || p.polpermissive::text || '|' ||
      coalesce(pg_get_expr(p.polqual,p.polrelid),'') || '|' ||
      coalesce(pg_get_expr(p.polwithcheck,p.polrelid),''), E'\n'
      ORDER BY r.relname COLLATE "C", p.polname COLLATE "C"), 'none'))
      FROM relations r JOIN pg_policy p ON p.polrelid = r.oid) AS policies
)
SELECT 'schema_context' AS report,
  md5(current_database()) AS database_name_fingerprint,
  md5(concat_ws('|', current_database(),
    coalesce(inet_server_addr()::text, '<unix-socket>'),
    coalesce(inet_server_port()::text, '<unix-socket>'))) AS endpoint_fingerprint,
  transaction_timestamp() AS inventory_transaction_at,
  current_setting('server_version_num') AS server_version_num,
  current_setting('server_encoding') AS server_encoding,
  current_setting('transaction_read_only') AS transaction_read_only,
  current_setting('transaction_isolation') AS transaction_isolation,
  current_setting('row_security') AS row_security,
  (SELECT rolsuper FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user) AS role_is_superuser,
  (SELECT rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user) AS role_bypasses_rls,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM relations) AS actual_relations_expected_five,
  (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('table',relname,'rls',relrowsecurity,
    'force_rls',relforcerowsecurity,'owned_by_current_role',owned_by_current_role)
    ORDER BY relname) FROM relations) AS relation_flags,
  (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('table',relname,'column',attname,'type',type,'not_null',attnotnull)
    ORDER BY relname,attname) FROM column_shapes
    WHERE (relname = 'YoungEvent' AND attname IN ('id','youngId','organizerId','rawJson','upstreamOrganizerIds','upstreamSponsorIds'))
       OR (relname = 'YoungOrganizer' AND attname IN ('id','normalizedName'))
       OR (relname IN ('UserYoungOrganizerSubscription','UserYoungEventSubscription','YoungNotification')
           AND attname IN ('id','userId','youngId','organizerId'))) AS key_shapes,
  fingerprints.* FROM fingerprints;

-- 2. Aggregate cardinalities only. Permission/RLS errors invalidate completeness.
SELECT 'row_totals' AS report,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM public."YoungEvent") AS events,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM public."YoungOrganizer") AS organizer_entities,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM public."UserYoungOrganizerSubscription") AS organizer_follows,
  (SELECT count(DISTINCT "userId") FROM public."UserYoungOrganizerSubscription") AS organizer_follow_users,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM public."UserYoungEventSubscription") AS direct_event_subscriptions,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM public."YoungNotification") AS notifications;

-- 3. Stored arrays: exact IDs only, never names; do not re-split strings or normalize identities.
-- The importer already discards duplicate/blank CSV tokens; zero anomalies here do not prove upstream lacked them.
WITH arrays AS (
  SELECT 'organizer'::text AS field, "upstreamOrganizerIds" AS ids FROM public."YoungEvent"
  UNION ALL SELECT 'sponsor', "upstreamSponsorIds" FROM public."YoungEvent"
), measured AS (
  SELECT field, cardinality(ids) AS slots,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM unnest(ids) AS u(v) WHERE v IS NULL) AS null_slots,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM unnest(ids) AS u(v) WHERE v = '') AS empty_slots,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM unnest(ids) AS u(v) WHERE v <> '' AND btrim(v) = '') AS ascii_space_slots,
    (SELECT count(v) - count(DISTINCT v) FROM unnest(ids) AS u(v)) AS duplicate_nonnull_slots
  FROM arrays
)
SELECT 'saved_arrays' AS report, field,
  CASE WHEN slots IS NULL THEN 'null_array' WHEN slots = 0 THEN 'zero' WHEN slots = 1 THEN 'one' ELSE 'multiple' END AS cardinality,
  count(*) AS event_rows, sum(null_slots) AS null_slots, sum(empty_slots) AS empty_slots,
  sum(ascii_space_slots) AS ascii_space_slots, sum(duplicate_nonnull_slots) AS duplicate_nonnull_slots,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE duplicate_nonnull_slots > 0) AS events_with_duplicates
FROM measured GROUP BY field, cardinality ORDER BY field, cardinality;

-- 4. Raw provenance shape, including scalar/non-object rawJson and absent versus explicit JSON null.
-- rawJson is upstreamColumns(row), excluding snapshot bookkeeping, before organizer/sponsor fallback.
WITH shapes AS (
  SELECT jsonb_typeof(e."rawJson") AS raw_type, k.key,
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(e."rawJson") IS DISTINCT FROM 'object' THEN 'raw_not_object'
         WHEN NOT (e."rawJson" ? k.key) THEN 'absent'
         ELSE jsonb_typeof(e."rawJson" -> k.key) END AS value_type,
    e."rawJson" -> k.key AS value
  FROM public."YoungEvent" e CROSS JOIN
    (VALUES ('organizer'),('organizer_dictText'),('sponsor'),('sponsor_dictText')) AS k(key)
)
SELECT 'raw_shapes' AS report, raw_type, key, value_type, count(*) AS event_rows,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE value_type = 'string' AND value #>> '{}' = '') AS empty_strings,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE value_type = 'string' AND value #>> '{}' <> '' AND btrim(value #>> '{}') = '') AS ascii_space_strings,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE value_type = 'array' AND jsonb_array_length(CASE WHEN value_type = 'array' THEN value ELSE '[]'::jsonb END) = 0) AS empty_arrays
FROM shapes GROUP BY raw_type,key,value_type ORDER BY raw_type,key,value_type;

-- 5. Array element kinds and exact duplicate/blank STRING elements if a raw field actually is an array.
-- No implicit JavaScript String(array) reconstruction and no positional ID/name pairing.
WITH raw_arrays AS (
  SELECT e.id, k.key, e."rawJson" -> k.key AS value
  FROM public."YoungEvent" e CROSS JOIN
    (VALUES ('organizer'),('organizer_dictText'),('sponsor'),('sponsor_dictText')) AS k(key)
  WHERE jsonb_typeof(e."rawJson") = 'object' AND jsonb_typeof(e."rawJson" -> k.key) = 'array'
), elements AS (
  SELECT a.id,a.key,v.value,jsonb_typeof(v.value) AS element_type
  FROM raw_arrays a CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(a.value) AS v(value)
), groups AS (
  SELECT id,key,element_type,count(*) AS slots,count(DISTINCT value) AS distinct_values,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE element_type = 'string' AND btrim(value #>> '{}') = '') AS blank_strings
  FROM elements GROUP BY id,key,element_type
)
SELECT 'raw_array_elements' AS report,key,element_type,count(*) AS event_rows,
  sum(slots) AS slots,sum(slots-distinct_values) AS exact_duplicate_slots,sum(blank_strings) AS blank_string_slots
FROM groups GROUP BY key,element_type ORDER BY key,element_type;

-- 6. Local-to-source ambiguity. Multi-source edges are observations, NOT atomic identity assignments.
-- "single_saved_source" is only a candidate: authoritative dictionary/provenance verification is still needed.
WITH event_sources AS (
  SELECT e.id,e."organizerId",array(SELECT DISTINCT v FROM unnest(e."upstreamOrganizerIds") AS u(v)
    WHERE v IS NOT NULL AND btrim(v) <> '') AS source_ids
  FROM public."YoungEvent" e
), observed AS (
  SELECT 'all_saved_sources'::text AS evidence,e."organizerId" AS local_id,u.source_id
  FROM event_sources e CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(e.source_ids) AS u(source_id)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'single_saved_source',e."organizerId",e.source_ids[1]
  FROM event_sources e WHERE cardinality(e.source_ids) = 1
), per_local AS (
  SELECT k.evidence,o.id AS local_id,count(DISTINCT v.source_id) AS linked
  FROM public."YoungOrganizer" o
  CROSS JOIN (VALUES ('all_saved_sources'),('single_saved_source')) AS k(evidence)
  LEFT JOIN observed v ON v.local_id = o.id AND v.evidence = k.evidence
  GROUP BY k.evidence,o.id
), per_source AS (
  SELECT evidence,source_id,count(DISTINCT local_id) AS linked FROM observed GROUP BY evidence,source_id
), summary AS (
  SELECT 'local_to_source' AS direction,evidence,linked FROM per_local
  UNION ALL SELECT 'source_to_local',evidence,linked FROM per_source
)
SELECT 'identity_ambiguity' AS report,direction,evidence,
  CASE WHEN linked = 0 THEN 'zero' WHEN linked = 1 THEN 'one' ELSE 'multiple' END AS counterpart_count,count(*) AS identities
FROM summary GROUP BY direction,evidence,counterpart_count ORDER BY direction,evidence,counterpart_count;

-- 7. Provenance eligibility counts only; labels remain opaque and no NFKC/CSV pairing is invented.
WITH evidence AS (
  SELECT e."organizerId", cardinality(e."upstreamOrganizerIds") AS saved_slots,
    jsonb_typeof(e."rawJson" -> 'organizer_dictText') AS organizer_label_type,
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(e."rawJson" -> 'organizer_dictText') = 'string'
      THEN btrim(e."rawJson" ->> 'organizer_dictText') <> '' ELSE false END AS organizer_label_nonempty,
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(e."rawJson" -> 'sponsor_dictText') = 'string'
      THEN btrim(e."rawJson" ->> 'sponsor_dictText') <> '' ELSE false END AS sponsor_label_nonempty
  FROM public."YoungEvent" e
)
SELECT 'provenance_candidates_not_verified' AS report,
  CASE WHEN organizer_label_nonempty THEN 'organizer_string_present'
       WHEN organizer_label_type IS NOT NULL AND organizer_label_type NOT IN ('string','null') THEN 'nonstring_organizer_unresolved'
       WHEN sponsor_label_nonempty THEN 'sponsor_only_string_candidate'
       ELSE 'no_nonempty_string_label' END AS label_evidence,
  CASE WHEN saved_slots IS NULL THEN 'null_array' WHEN saved_slots = 0 THEN 'zero' WHEN saved_slots = 1 THEN 'one' ELSE 'multiple' END AS saved_cardinality,
  ("organizerId" IS NOT NULL) AS linked_local_entity,count(*) AS event_rows
FROM evidence GROUP BY label_evidence,saved_cardinality,linked_local_entity
ORDER BY label_evidence,saved_cardinality,linked_local_entity;

-- 8. Follow exposure of legacy multi-source CANDIDATES, without expanding any follow.
-- Candidate means a local scalar organizer linked from an event with >1 distinct saved nonblank source ID.
WITH candidates AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT e."organizerId" AS id FROM public."YoungEvent" e
  WHERE e."organizerId" IS NOT NULL AND
    (SELECT count(DISTINCT v) FROM unnest(e."upstreamOrganizerIds") AS u(v)
     WHERE v IS NOT NULL AND btrim(v) <> '') > 1
)
SELECT 'legacy_multi_source_candidate_exposure' AS report,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM candidates) AS candidate_entities,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM public."YoungEvent" e JOIN candidates c ON c.id = e."organizerId") AS linked_events,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM public."UserYoungOrganizerSubscription" s JOIN candidates c ON c.id = s."organizerId") AS organizer_follow_rows,
  (SELECT count(DISTINCT s."userId") FROM public."UserYoungOrganizerSubscription" s JOIN candidates c ON c.id = s."organizerId") AS distinct_follow_users,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM public."UserYoungEventSubscription" s JOIN public."YoungEvent" e ON e."youngId" = s."youngId"
    JOIN candidates c ON c.id = e."organizerId") AS separate_direct_event_subscription_rows;

-- 9. Notifications: finite kind/read/expiry/association buckets, no IDs/title/body/dedupeKey output.
-- Notifications have nullable scalar IDs but no Prisma organizer/event FK relation; inventory dangling references explicitly.
WITH candidates AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT e."organizerId" AS id FROM public."YoungEvent" e
  WHERE e."organizerId" IS NOT NULL AND
    (SELECT count(DISTINCT v) FROM unnest(e."upstreamOrganizerIds") AS u(v)
     WHERE v IS NOT NULL AND btrim(v) <> '') > 1
), classified AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN n.kind IN ('event_changed','signup_open','signup_deadline','event_start','organizer_digest')
         THEN n.kind ELSE 'other_unrecognized_kind' END AS kind,
    (n."readAt" IS NOT NULL) AS is_read,
    CASE WHEN n."expiresAt" IS NULL THEN 'no_expiry'
         WHEN n."expiresAt" <= transaction_timestamp() THEN 'expired' ELSE 'future' END AS expiry,
    CASE WHEN n."organizerId" IS NULL THEN 'no_organizer'
         WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public."YoungOrganizer" o WHERE o.id = n."organizerId") THEN 'dangling_organizer'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM candidates c WHERE c.id = n."organizerId") THEN 'legacy_multi_source_candidate'
         ELSE 'other_existing_organizer' END AS organizer_association,
    CASE WHEN n."youngId" IS NULL THEN 'no_event'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public."YoungEvent" e WHERE e."youngId" = n."youngId") THEN 'existing_event'
         ELSE 'dangling_event' END AS event_association
  FROM public."YoungNotification" n
)
SELECT 'notification_aggregates' AS report,kind,is_read,expiry,organizer_association,event_association,count(*) AS notifications
FROM classified GROUP BY kind,is_read,expiry,organizer_association,event_association
ORDER BY kind,is_read,expiry,organizer_association,event_association;

ROLLBACK;
```

</details>

Authoritative dictionary evidence: the existing normal SSO/TOTP and Young session preparation were reused for a single successful browser-helper GET to `/sysdepart/sysDepart/queryTreeList`. The original session-visible response is 2,117,024 bytes, SHA256 `4fc1f9b7722d78fb5b589bd4d9e44b0e69424552ba77527f68ac22a079359e05`, retained privately with mode 0600. Its 3,079 string IDs are unique; each node’s `id`, `key` and `value` agree exactly, and every non-root `parentId` matches the actual tree parent. Titles equal `departName`, but eleven title groups contain distinct IDs (four groups even share a parent), confirming that display-name uniqueness cannot define source identity. No aliases, campus-wide completeness or cross-tenant/global ID scope are inferred.

In the already retained twenty-row live first-page sample, all 24 distinct organizer IDs (27 occurrences) and all 12 distinct sponsor IDs (28 occurrences) independently match the dictionary. Looking up names by source ID and then joining the resulting titles agrees with each role’s existing display string for all twenty sampled rows. This is a bounded forward lookup observation, not a universal ordering or scalar-splitting contract; neither names nor normalized names are used to pair or merge identities. The next input slice needs reproducible dictionary provenance and freshness before canonical identity/read/follow activation. The fixed production aggregate inventory in #1592 remains unchanged and has not yet been executed.

issue.title: fix(overview): expose pending activity reads while a focus is visible
issue.body:
The Home overview can appear ready while its nested personal-calendar read is still pending. `HomePersonalOverview` marks its own viewer read complete before `OverviewTab` finishes `fetchPersonalCalendar`. `OverviewFocusCard` renders the loading status only when no other focus item exists, so an already-visible class hides the activity-loading indication. The existing `overview.activity-owner-transition` rule requires unresolved activity reads to show loading and avoid claiming an empty agenda.

This was found while validating PR #1564 against main #1572. Two original 19-case batches retained 10 passes, one failure and eight unexecuted cases each. The first failure was an independently confirmed immediate-URL assertion racing native MCP client navigation. After correcting that consumer, the next failure was the original Home footer bottom predicate at 390 px, before the MCP portion ran.

The retained second trace shows the single native Control+End at 89893.649 ms while the real calendar read (89855.568–89924.054 ms) was pending. A later snapshot inserts the three Demo activities 28/30/31 into the upcoming section. A separate unchanged-assertion observation passed and measured Home growing from 4738 to 4912 px after the main overview was rendered; this supports late layout as the footer failure mechanism, but the failed trace lacks per-region heights. The passing observation is not a repaired-product result and does not prove Tailwind caused or excluded the timing.

Acceptance:

- Retain the current class/focus while the real nested calendar response is held; visibly and accessibly expose the pending activity read even when another focus exists.
- Expose the actual overview busy state until its nested read finishes; retain existing ownership, cancellation, failure/retry and empty-agenda behavior.
- Hold and release an actual Worker response in native browser validation, independently verify pending and completed states, and preserve matched original screenshots for the changed loading presentation.
- Make the footer consumer wait for the actual overview readiness before its one native Control+End; preserve every original scroll-container bottom assertion, timeout, deadline, business and side-effect guard.
- Retain exact awaited native URL assertions for both MCP client changes; do not add sleeps, retries, DOM scrolling or relaxed budgets.
- Complete independent review and full current-head CI before merge. Keep original failures separate from successful validation.

Part of #1155; this does not complete the suite-wide migration or authorize production Demo activation.

issue.title: fix(admin): align clear suspension badges with user roles
issue.body:
On the desktop `/admin/users` table, an unsuspended user's status badge sits above the role badge. `AdminUsersDesktopTable` always renders a secondary `TruncatedText`; a null value creates an empty second line, even though the table cells already use middle alignment.

Render the secondary suspension explanation only for an active suspension. Keep timed and permanent explanations, mobile layout, and shared `TruncatedText` behavior unchanged. Verify the real admin page in English and Chinese: the clear-status and role badge centers differ by at most 1 CSS pixel, and active suspension groups remain centered with their full explanation.

issue.title: feat(navigation): 统一桌面 Sidebar 与移动 TabBar 的导航层级
issue.body:
## 目标：跨端共用一套导航心智模型

桌面 Sidebar 的一级入口对应移动端底部 TabBar：命名、顺序、功能归属和选中状态一致。不要让用户在不同设备或不同入口重新理解另一套目录。二级导航也要有明确的跨端对应关系。

## 已确认的产品规则

- 一级目录及各 Tab 不再提供目录折叠/展开按钮；原有日程、课程、校园、活动等分组不能因历史折叠偏好隐藏。
- 进入页面后使用子 Sidebar，并能返回上一层。本地提供根 Sidebar 预览，无需刷新页面才能切换导航层级。
- 删除 AI 助手（MCP）旁的说明文案、日历等项目旁的说明 icon 和对应解释入口。数量提示保留数字即可。
- 管理区的页面层级也始终展开，继续遵循现有权限可见性。
- 核心不是只删几个按钮，而是降低层级理解成本、减少桌面/移动及各位置之间的不一致。

## 已确认的一级入口与归属

一级入口与移动底部 Tab 统一为 **工作台 / 日历 / 校园 / 活动**，顺序一致。课程订阅是工作台中的功能，不独立占据一级入口。

| 一级入口 | 功能归属 |
| --- | --- |
| 工作台 | 个人概览、作业、待办、考试、课程订阅，以及活动关注和通知 |
| 日历 | 个人日历；沿用现有登录、数据权限和日历来源规则 |
| 校园 | 公开教学班、课程、教师目录，以及校车、天气、新闻、教室、校园网站等公共资源 |
| 活动 | 公开活动、活动日历、主办单位及详情；个人活动关注与通知放在工作台 |

设置、我的上传及管理入口等从用户头像访问，不作为根 Sidebar 目录或底部一级 Tab。管理入口继续严格按权限可见。工具与集成说明保留可发现入口，但不占一级导航。

根 Sidebar 仅呈现当前层级；不直接展开下一层内容。例如校车的“路线图”不再内嵌于校车下方，进入校车后再显示其时刻表、路线图等同级页面。课程、新闻、活动及管理队列等类似目录使用相同的子 Sidebar 模型，不能只给少数页面特殊处理。子 Sidebar 返回上一层为本地导航预览，不刷新当前内容、不丢失未保存输入或修改 URL/history；选择真实目的地才执行正常路由导航。

保留既有深链接、查询参数、片段、匿名/登录/管理员可见性及 Demo 投影。既有 /workspace/uploads 等路径保留兼容，但入口属于头像菜单。公开目录中不混放个人课程订阅或活动关注/通知入口。

## 二级呈现方案

- 桌面的二级目的地由当前层平铺子 Sidebar 呈现；移动 Web 从顶部菜单打开同源的当前层平铺 Drawer，底部固定四个一级入口。本地返回或预览上级时 Drawer 保持打开，选择真实目的地后才关闭并导航。原生 App 在当前 Tab 内使用功能目录及详情返回路径，对应相同的功能归属。
- 从详情查看上级根 Sidebar 是本地导航状态：保留当前内容页，展示已经拥有的根目录预览；无需刷新或重新请求页面数据。选择目的地时才进行正常客户端路由导航。
- 页面详情使用其真实集合父级；资源详情与页面内锚点不挤进一级 Tab。当前层目录平铺展示，不再内嵌下一层子树；管理队列进入对应子 Sidebar 后平铺呈现，保留权限上下文。
- Web 同级路由导航由桌面 Sidebar 与移动 Drawer 共同承担，使用同一份目录和当前态；页面内锚点继续使用独立的页面目录。

## 验收

- 对应的桌面/移动一级入口具有相同的名称、顺序、功能归属和当前态；从首页、搜索或深链接进入同一功能时，归属不矛盾。
- 根导航 → 子导航 → 返回/预览上一级流程清楚可用，本地预览不刷新页面。
- 不再出现上述目录或管理层级的折叠按钮、隐形折叠动作和历史隐藏状态；说明入口移除后，数字提示仍正确。
- 保留权限、正常导航、键盘/触屏可用性，以及晚到数量更新后当前项仍可见的已有保证。
- 同步规范和回归测试，提供相同可见数据、语言和视口的原生对照；独立审查与当前提交 CI 通过后交付。

本规则更新此前 [PR #1520](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/pull/1520) 的相关折叠与说明交互。现有移动端基线见 `iOS/Views/Shared/ContentViewTab.swift`；跨端页面归属与二级呈现应一并核对。

## 交付证据

Web 的统一导航已通过 [PR #1596](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/pull/1596) 交付：完整 48 项检查通过，4,846 项单元测试通过，生产环境已核实运行合并提交 3c1fc2dcb604。当前层平铺 Sidebar、移动 Drawer 和本地返回预览共用目录，个人订阅与公开页面按上述规则分区。

iOS 的统一导航已通过 [PR #166](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/pull/166) 交付：合并提交 f50783cde541 的源码树与已验收版本完全一致。手机、平板各 426 项单元测试和原有 71 个 UI 用例全成功、零跳过，各 93/93 个原生场景齐全；四个截图任务与完整 44 张原图通过。App/Widget 的已签名测试包为 3.0.0 / 20261114.010238。

两端 PR 均保留经过独立实看的原始前后对照及验证链接。原生合并后的 [自动 TestFlight 流水线](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/43471125069) 单独继续跟踪；此处完成的是统一导航的实现、验证与合并。

issue.title: feat(demo): browse existing API reference without request execution
issue.body:
Part of #548. Support reading the existing API reference in Demo; do not grant API authority or introduce a separate documentation UI.

## Acceptance

- Reuse `/api/docs`, its existing canonical redirect and `/api/docs/{path}` navigation, localized copy and the existing current OpenAPI document. Keep ordinary documentation and the normative contract unchanged.
- Allow only the exact trusted Demo GET/HEAD/page-data/spec reads required for browsing. Define and verify the actual local-spec delivery policy before implementation: exercise owned ASSETS (or a proven no-binding local source), account explicitly for any permitted local-static binding reads, and prove no external origin, DB/KV/R2 or other business reads. Do not infer zero I/O from the static SSR loader or hide ASSETS calls from observations.
- Guard the actual Scalar reference so Demo cannot authorize, retain real credentials, choose an external server or execute requests, including read requests. Disabling agent/MCP/persisted auth alone is insufficient. No fake principal, SDK authentication bypass or production flag change.
- Keep tag/operation/model reading and navigation usable. Clear retired interactive/auth state across ordinary-to-Demo, locale and exit/re-entry transitions; unknown paths, expired/mixed identities, writes and unrelated API calls remain fail-closed.

## Validation

Independent source and current Scalar-contract review; real owned spec/ASSETS and boundary HTTP controls, request-execution/outbound observations, normal-reader compatibility and same-page lifecycle controls; targeted bilingual desktop/phone reading and native visual evidence. Preserve budgets and original test deadlines. This is the existing readonly requirement, not a new product decision.

issue.title: feat(demo): support existing read-only legal and usage guides
issue.body:
Part of #548. Make existing informational pages usable from the Demo shell without changing their real legal or instructional content.

## Acceptance

- Reuse `/terms`, `/privacy`, `/guides/markdown-support` and `/usage/mobile`, `/usage/bot`, `/usage/cli`, `/usage/mcp` with their existing localized content and local illustrations. Retain `/community/comments/guide` as its existing redirect. Do not fictionalize terms, privacy policy or installation instructions, and do not add a new help/workbench UI.
- Admit only the required GET/HEAD, page-data and exact redirect destinations after trusted Demo identity validation. Preserve the existing MCP client selection query. Writes and unrelated OAuth/admin/settings/upload families remain blocked; normal readers remain unchanged.
- Preserve local reading interactions, language changes and copy-to-clipboard. Real external authorization, installation, download/store and group-join actions stay disabled with an accessible explanation in Demo; do not execute commands or open those flows on behalf of the reader.
- Keep Demo/read-only identity clear without altering the source documents. Guard identity/locale transitions so a retired ordinary document or response does not restore active controls.

## Validation

Independent source review; owned SSR/page-data/HEAD/redirect and invalid-identity controls; precise denied-write checks and no business/external I/O; representative bilingual desktop/phone reading, copy and transition controls with native visual evidence. Keep the production Demo flag unchanged. API reference browsing is a separate leaf.

## Validation

Independent source review; pure graph/count/date controls; real owned Worker SSR/API known and foreign positive/negative controls, write rejection and effects/state invariants; targeted identity/locale browser controls and native desktop/phone visual evidence. No production Demo enablement.

issue.title: chore(todo): record sanitized list-read failure categories
issue.body:
Part of #233. The retained historical Todo-list failure does not identify its layer. Existing safe operation logs cannot distinguish HTTP/authentication/JSON failures, and the available operational log window contains no matching Todo phase evidence.

## Scope

Observe the final result of the existing Todo read without changing the SDK request, retry, token-refresh, filtering, rendering or completion-write control flow. On failure, emit only a fixed operation and finite phase/outcome/reason labels derived from typed errors or directly known boundaries. Preserve an honest unspecified/unknown category where request/body/decode/projection distinctions were discarded by the current SDK.

## Acceptance

- Use typed errors and sentinels only; do not classify from raw message strings. The classifier must not call `Error()` to inspect content.
- No raw error text, HTTP body/path/URL, user/message IDs, titles, query/filter values, filenames, tokens or payloads enter the new metadata. Keep emitted values finite and bounded.
- Preserve the exact existing returned error and user-facing behavior, read attempts/cancellation/budgets, token refresh, and at-most-once uncertain writes. Logging observes the final existing read only; it must not start work or add per-attempt retries.
- Test sensitive-error inputs and the real retained Todo-read failure/success boundaries, including cancellation and no added calls. Keep generated SDK files unchanged and avoid adding a logging framework.
- Complete independent review, appropriate local verification and current-head CI before merging.

This slice prepares safe evidence for a future natural failure. It does not recover the historical cause, close #233, or authorize a production cutover.

issue.title: fix(rooms): avoid revalidating normalized codes as raw input
issue.body:
## Problem

The existing ordinary room-map REST adapter can return HTTP 500 for input accepted by its own declared schema. For example, `ﬄ` repeated 22 times has raw length 22 but normalizes to 66 ASCII letters. `Ⅷ` repeated 17 times similarly normalizes from 17 to 68 characters.

The current `roomCodeSchema` applies the 64-character limit before NFKC/uppercase. The adapter validates and transforms the input, then passes the transformed string into `getRoomMap`, which validates again; lookup can parse it again as well. A subsequent raw-length check throws instead of returning the supported unknown-room result. Direct execution of the existing REST adapter reproduced HTTP 500; no production request or database/upstream probe was made.

The new Demo adapter in #1544 had the same repeated-normalization risk and is being corrected there to preserve raw input after the adapter's validation. The inherited ordinary path remains separate.

## Acceptance

- Trace REST, GraphQL, MCP, Web, iCal and service callers and prevent transformed output from being incorrectly revalidated as a new raw input.
- Preserve the current accepted raw-input set, raw length limit, trim/NFKC/uppercase behavior, supported map lookup and protocol error semantics. Do not reject valid expanded input merely to avoid the 500.
- Invalid raw inputs still fail validation; full-width known room codes still resolve correctly; valid expanded unknown codes retain each interface's normal unknown-room result instead of throwing.
- Verify through real supported entrypoints with owned static inputs, retaining independent expected results, no unexpected writes, cleanup and relevant ordinary regressions.
- Independent review and current-head CI before delivery. Do not use a blanket catch or invented room result to hide an error.

## Confirmed call sites

The ordinary REST adapter, GraphQL input boundary and MCP input schema all pass normalized output to the service, which normalizes again before lookup. The service also reparses at lookup. Schedule and exam iCal builders similarly pass `safeParse(...).data` to a raw-input lookup. Web lookup links/submission and the shared preview normalize before sending the request, which can independently turn a valid raw input into an overlong request. These entrypoints must preserve the same accepted raw-input set; a service-only change would leave the browser defect in place.

The Demo adapter correction and its expanded-input HTTP checks remain in #1544; this issue covers the inherited ordinary paths. The response schema already accepts the normalized code as a string, so it does not need a new output-length restriction.

issue.title: fix(db): recognize wrapped PostgreSQL serialization conflicts
issue.body:
The Permissions job on PR #1547 exposed a retry-classification gap unrelated to room normalization.

Observed head: `1ec28ed4be906d35c4fd8b79470bd2ff60956f4c`. Original [run 42503014610, job 128799621454](https://github.com/Life-USTC/server/actions/runs/42503014610/job/128799621454): 105 tests passed and one failed in `tests/integration/user-rls.test.ts:337`, “preserves actor-aware token creation, public projections and account-deletion cascades”. The failure occurs in `deleteOwnAccount` through `runSerializableTransaction`.

Prisma 7.10.1 reports this raw-query serialization conflict as `P2010`, with `meta.driverAdapterError.cause.kind = TransactionWriteConflict` and `originalCode = 40001`. The current classifier recognizes `P2034` or a driver error along `cause`, but does not inspect this exact wrapped adapter path. This is not the unresolved P2028 startup investigation in #1465, and it does not establish which concurrent operation caused the database conflict.

Fix the narrow classification while retaining the existing three-attempt transaction budget. Recognize only the documented adapter write-conflict shape and supported PostgreSQL SQLSTATEs, never arbitrary P2010 errors or message substrings. Cause inspection must terminate on cycles and avoid invoking accessors. Preserve non-retry error identity and all account-deletion/ownership guards.

Acceptance:
- A realistic Prisma P2010/DriverAdapterError envelope for 40001 retries within the existing limit, and succeeds when the subsequent attempt succeeds.
- P2034 and supported direct/cause adapter conflicts remain recognized; unrelated raw errors, constraints and misleading messages do not retry.
- Cycles/accessors terminate safely; exhaustion remains three attempts and rethrows the original terminal error.
- The original account-deletion RLS case retains its complete assertions and is verified with the current source; no blind workflow rerun or weakened timeout/guard substitutes for the fix.

Part of #601 (the existing Task's account-deletion and cascade acceptance).

Primary contract evidence: [Prisma transaction conflicts](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/queries/transactions#transaction-timing-issues), the installed 7.10.1 `@prisma/adapter-pg` 40001/40P01 mapping, and its `DriverAdapterError.cause` types. Original failure logs are retained locally without publishing query parameters or private fixture data.

issue.title: feat(demo): support existing activity subscriptions and notifications
issue.body:
## Problem

Demo readers can browse public Young events and organizers, but the existing personal activity-subscription and notification pages remain blocked. Their ordinary GET implementation refreshes notifications and can update subscriptions, create/delete notifications and invalidate calendar exports. Calling it and filtering the result would violate the Demo boundary.

Part of #548. Extend the existing `/workspace/subscriptions/activities` page and its current events, organizers and notifications views; do not create a separate Demo dashboard.

## Acceptance

- Trusted Demo branches run before ordinary authentication/database/refresh services in page/data, event and organizer subscription list/state reads, and notification reads. Existing query schemas, page limits, default/unknown view behavior and out-of-range redirects remain consistent with ordinary interfaces.
- Reuse the existing 42 fictional events and 22 organizers. One pure fixed membership/notification graph drives private lists, public detail subscription facts, unread navigation counts and the Young entries in the existing personal calendar. Do not introduce a real principal or read real private preferences.
- Include 21 event subscriptions, 21 organizer subscriptions and 23 fixed notifications (21 unread and two read) so the existing 20-row views and unread filter have real continuation pages. Use the fixed Demo clock, independent of wall time. Reminder flags, source-missing changes, reminder kinds and timestamps must agree with the referenced records and expiration rules; never suggest a collector or notification delivery ran.
- Where needed, adjust a non-Home event in the existing graph to provide an honest current signup/deadline/start reminder example, and set justified fixed source-creation facts for the organizer digest. Preserve the first five Home activities' title, dates and order. Do not invent a second event graph or change ordinary notification rules.
- Add the subscribed Young records to the existing calendar projection; calendar APIs, navigation counts and Home summaries must derive from that combined graph. Update previous fixed-count expectations rather than leaving a contradictory nine-item calendar.
- Reuse existing page controls for views, All/Unread, paging and internal detail/calendar navigation. Clearly label fictional read-only facts. Existing subscription controls and mark-read actions remain disabled natively and guarded in handlers; all subscription PUT and mark-read POST requests remain rejected. Enable the now-supported internal Manage navigation without opening external registration or other side effects.
- Retire old private data, notifications and counts on mode, locale, owner or expiry changes. Real held ordinary responses, same-page transitions, native locale reload and exit/re-entry must not restore prior private rows or badge counts.
- Verify exact SSR/data/API schemas and pagination, shared detail/calendar/count facts, actual owned ordinary positive controls followed by Demo isolation, zero Demo effects and unchanged database snapshots with cleanup. Exercise existing desktop/phone UI, actual continuation and unread filtering; preserve ordinary subscription/mark-read behavior, retries and authorization.
- Capture native before/after evidence, independently review source and visuals, and pass current-head CI before merging. No new acceptance directories or framework; use existing tests and temporary artifacts.

issue.body:
Part of native parent #107 (`test(ios): verify parity and release the aligned app`); related capability parent #101 remains open.

The natural [main CI 42491355510](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/42491355510), source `a2ab21df9cd4b696b96447cefe869a2ec7b7d0e4`, completed with two native UI failures. Original plans establish **423 unit successes and 70/71 UI successes, zero skips, on each device**. All 71 cases executed. Both jobs exited with the original `xcodebuild` status 65 after assertion failures; approximately 90/94-minute jobs were below the unchanged 120-minute job limit.

### Original failure boundaries

- **iPhone:** `E2ETests.testFeaturesTabShowsAllFeatures`, [original job/log](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/42491355510/job/128764224360). `selectTab("Features")` made one `square.grid.2x2` tap, then found no `discover_university` and entered `navigateBack`; [E2ETests.swift:141](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/blob/a2ab21df9cd4b696b96447cefe869a2ec7b7d0e4/Tests/Life-USTC-UITests/E2ETests.swift#L141) failed its existing five-second back-control existence wait. The final original AX shows **Home selected**, not Discover. It does not establish a missing back button on Discover or the cause of the unsuccessful tab transition.
- **iPad:** `YoungCampusJourneyTests.testActivityFiltersApplyCancelClearAndPreserveUnknownDateContext`, [original job/log](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/42491355510/job/128764224280). At [line 66](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/blob/a2ab21df9cd4b696b96447cefe869a2ec7b7d0e4/Tests/Life-USTC-UITests/YoungCampusJourneyTests.swift#L66), opening `young.filters.active` timed out in the existing ten-second `enabled && hittable` readiness guard. Date-range value 1 and date-picker existence had passed. The readiness evaluation contains two native Find operations lasting about 6.694 and 2.092 seconds; it does not record their boolean results. The final original screenshot/AX shows the active control with value All, but this is after failure and does not prove it was hittable within the deadline. **The active option tap, Apply and expected `active=true` request were not reached**; no HTTP-active regression is established.

Original native artifacts are retained by that CI: iPhone `13624582666`, iPad `13624990975`. Gallery artifacts contain 93/93 iPhone and 91/93 iPad named PNGs, both correctly marked `ui_failure`; iPad lacks `YoungFilters` and `YoungFilteredUnknownDates` because execution stopped earlier. Failure media remain original CI artifacts rather than PR comparison images.

The aggregate native gate failed, so **Build IPA, Upload to TestFlight and Group were all skipped**. This run made no Apple upload attempt; its failure is not an Apple agreement error. The account holder has still not confirmed the separate agreement prerequisite.

### Completion criteria

- [ ] Establish the minimal actual app or driver correction from the original input, AX/activity/video and source evidence, followed by independent technical review before coding.
- [ ] Preserve all original 71 cases and business assertions, original per-step five/ten-second budgets, single actions/retry policy, fixtures and dependency pins. No blind rerun, added tap, weakened hittability guard or timeout increase.
- [ ] Verify the reviewed new source through its ordinary complete dual-device CI: exact unit/case plans, zero skips, all 93 original gallery states per device and the IPA gate. Preserve this failed run and its unknown-cause boundaries.

The accepted Sunday-calendar delivery remains recorded; no calendar-regression cause has been established. OAuth, Apple agreement and final TestFlight acceptance continue under the existing parent tasks, which remain open.

[PR #157](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/pull/157) delivered the bounded Young UI readiness-query correction as `cf8dd362`, with the exact accepted source tree. Its [full PR CI](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/42503252885) passed both original 423-unit/71-UI suites, zero skips, both 93-image galleries and signed App/Widget IPA `20261109.024011`; all original test IDs were retained. Both previously failing cases passed on this source, which does not establish their original causes. The [natural main CI](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/42514300727), exact source `cf8dd3626db7e4d760e1a9c252f3535a0a319c06`, subsequently failed: each device passed all 423 units and 70/71 UI cases with zero skips. Both original a2ab failures passed on this run; the new failures differ:

- iPhone [original job](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/42514300727/job/128833852805): `testActivityFilterOrganizerRetryAndEmptyResultRecovery`, line 136 → `chooseFilter` line 370. The organizer readiness predicate took 5.754 seconds and the single option tap took 8.824 seconds; the shared ten-second deadline expired before the selected-value wait, which had no recorded predicate evaluation. The final original AX and PNG show **Student Arts Association selected**. Module, Apply and the organizer-filtered request were not reached. This does not establish a production selection failure.
- iPad [original job](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/42514300727/job/128833852707): `testAccountManagementOpensSupportedWebsitePagesAndRefreshesProfileOnReturn`, first Profile webpage, line 55 → `closeWebsite` line 128. The enabled-filtered Close query’s live hittability Find took 9.190 seconds within the original ten-second readiness wait and timed out. **Close was never tapped**; no dismissal or profile-refresh defect is established. The final original AX/PNG contains one BrowserView and one Close, but does not establish period-time hittability.

Both galleries contain 93/93 required originals, correctly marked `ui_failure`; native failure skipped IPA, Upload and Group, so this run made no Apple upload attempt. The accepted PR’s corresponding cases passed with shorter measured query/input times. Runner image, Xcode and simulator runtime match, but no resource-pressure telemetry establishes VM contention. Query/driver candidates remain under source review; no timeout, action count or business assertion has been relaxed. #156, #107 and #101 remain open; real OAuth, confirmation of the Apple agreement and TestFlight acceptance remain unfinished.

[PR #159](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/pull/159), head `d77d579`, supplies exact organizer leaf IDs and a narrower scoped Safari Close query while preserving the original budgets, single inputs and business assertions. Its [natural full CI](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/43226603720) has passed both original native ID sets per device: 423 unit and 71 UI successes, zero skips, plus the aggregate native gate. Both 93-image galleries are complete/ui_success and all 186 native PNGs were byte/hash checked and fully decoded. Original activities confirm the leaf ID is exported and used. Organizer readiness/tap was observed at 0.400/2.664s and the first scoped Close Find at 1.597s; the retained selected-value and return/refresh assertions execute successfully. These observations do not establish Apple-internal or resource-contention causes. Signed App/Widget IPA `20261112.231437` has passed original byte/hash/CRC and official Mac deep/strict signature/entitlement verification. PR #159 is merged as `83d5e791`, with its exact accepted source tree. The [natural main CI](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/43249186909) has completed its native and signed-IPA acceptance; its TestFlight delivery status is recorded below. This issue and both parent tasks stay open: original root causes, real OAuth and TestFlight acceptance remain unfinished, and the Apple agreement has not been confirmed effective.


### Main acceptance and subsequent native failure — 2026-11-12 UTC

The original natural main run `43249186909`, exact `83d5e79168cae8e461d7260ac9f69711cfc0af2e`, passed **423 units and all original 71 UI cases per device, zero skips**, with the exact accepted test-ID sets. Both original galleries contain all 93 required PNGs, marked complete/ui_success with the exact source; ZIP digests/CRC and every PNG's full decode were verified. The original signed App/Widget IPA **3.0.0 / 20261113.011814** passed archive integrity and official Mac deep/strict code-signature, bundle/profile/entitlement checks. This proves acceptance of that source, without establishing the causes of earlier intermittent failures.

The original [Upload to TestFlight job 131359477289](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/43249186909/job/131359477289) was cancelled without a runner (`runner_id=0`, empty runner name and steps). Its check annotations explicitly report unavailable hosted runners and macOS arm64 capacity constraints. **No Apple upload or agreement request executed in this attempt**; Group was skipped. After native/IPA acceptance, the single authorized [targeted retry job 131373047684](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/43249186909/job/131373047684) acquired a runner and successfully downloaded the existing signed artifact. Its actual Apple upload failed with “A required agreement is missing or has expired.” Group was skipped. This attempt establishes an unresolved Apple agreement prerequisite, distinct from the first attempt’s runner-capacity failure. No full native/build rerun was requested, and no further upload retry will be attempted before the account holder confirms the agreement is handled. TestFlight distribution remains unaccepted.

The independent [PR #160 original full CI](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/43251357130) failed. Its iPad job was never allocated, while its iPhone actually executed all 71 UI cases: **70 successes, one failure, zero skips**. The sole failing case remains `AccountJourneyTests.testAccountManagementOpensSupportedWebsitePagesAndRefreshesProfileOnReturn`; this time it reached the fifth **authorizations** page (`/account/settings/authorizations`) after completing the preceding four pages. The expected website request and Close/browser existence checks passed. During the unchanged ten-second actionable-Close wait, a native Find took **9.316 seconds**; the wait failed before any Close tap on this page. The final original AX/PNG contains a single BrowserView and enabled Close, with the expected JSON response visible and no visible overlay, but does not record period-time hittability. This is a readiness failure, not evidence of a failed dismissal or refresh. The same source main iPhone case passed this same fifth page: its original actionable-Close evaluation took 0.502 seconds (Find 0.476 seconds), followed by the single successful 2.885-second Close tap. This establishes an observed query-time difference, without establishing Ruby, VM or animation causality.

PR #160 changes four Ruby action pins only: its app/test sources and native-test job block are byte-identical to main `83d5e791`. This narrows the source difference but does not excuse the failed run or establish VM contention. Its original failed payload, activities and media are preserved; no blind retry or guard/timeout relaxation has been made. This issue and parent tasks remain open pending a justified correction and the remaining OAuth/release acceptance.

### PR161 original Workspace readiness failures

On exact `10fb88463afb901270c43f439e9bb02358b0554b`, [natural CI 43304086404](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/43304086404) retained all original IDs. Official plans establish 423 Unit successes per device; iPad passed all 71 UI cases, while iPhone had 69 successes and two failures, with zero skips. This continues the existing readiness investigation rather than establishing a new product regression.

- `testHomeworkCompletionUsesServerTimestampAndTAHasNoManualAction`, caller line188 → `open` line294: final control-existence check passed; the original ten-second `enabled && hittable` wait for `home_homeworks` failed after native Finds of 5.257s and 3.000s. The control was never tapped; no homework GET/PUT occurred, so completion/timestamp/TA assertions were not reached.
- `testSubscribedExamsRetainUnknownDatesAndLinkUsingSectionJWID`, caller line224 → the same helper: existence passed, but the original readiness wait for `workspace.exam.702` failed with Finds of 7.715s and 1.500s. The correct exams GET included `includeDateUnknown=true`; the target was not tapped, so detail/JWID assertions were not reached.

The original final AX snapshots show the correct unique target in Home/Exams, but were recorded 4.887s/6.566s after failure. They do not record period-time enabled/hittable values or establish occlusion, scheduler/SDK, dependency or business causality. Phone exported90/93 required originals; iPad exported93/93. The supplemental identity matrix was skipped through its native dependency; IPA acceptance was not reached. Original evidence remains in the [Phone artifact](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/43304086404/artifacts/13990863292). No deadline, query, input or business assertion has been changed or rerun; this issue and parent tasks remain open.


[PR #161](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/pull/161), head `7702c9620968ef8e37915e5b1b309df7d8b55022`, now adds independently reviewed, bounded observation to just these two Workspace readiness waits. It preserves the original format predicate/element, ten-second waiter, polling and single tap; only monotonic start/end/outcome and the public handler's first **observed combined-true** timestamp are stored, with no handler UI reads and attachment only in teardown. It cannot expose false polls, individual properties or per-Find cost; callback/start ordering and pre-installation success limit interpretation, and clock/lock work has nonzero cost. Actual existing Beta27 simulator build-for-testing passed (46.547s; no native test or signing); formal-toolchain/full-suite acceptance remains pending. This does not fix or establish the cause of the original two failures, replace the skipped identity matrix, or close this issue or its parent tasks. Current natural CI: [Screenshots](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/43333025595) (queued); [CI](https://github.com/Life-USTC/Life-USTC/actions/runs/43333025546) (queued). No manual CI retry, dispatch or release action was requested.


Dependency provenance scope on current `7702c962`: native records its post-UI resolution; each supplemental job resolves independently and checks only its own before/after file; IPA is a separate checkout/cache/resolve. These records do **not** currently bind the three stages to one dependency graph. No actual cross-job drift has been established. The current natural run remains useful evidence for its own source and executions; it cannot establish that cross-stage dependency chain. A future reviewed source would need explicit same-run native-lock consumption and fail-closed tuple checks. No current test, budget, source or CI operation is changed by this clarification.

## 目标

补齐 #548 的现有 `/catalog/rooms` 教室目录与地图查询。当前演示身份在请求边界被拒绝；普通读取会访问远程地图清单、图片及数据库，不能直接放开。

## 验收

- 复用现有楼栋/楼层目录、房间查询、地图预览、缩放与复位；固定虚构教室覆盖 highlighted、overview、unavailable 三种真实协议状态。
- 目录、页面数据、`/api/catalog/rooms/[code]/map` 和本地示意图形成同一闭合图；保留原 roomCode 的 NFKC、大小写、空白及校验语义。未知或真实代码不能回落到普通服务。
- 图片明确为演示示意图，不代表学校实际布局。只允许闭合图关联的同源只读图像；真实外部地图链接禁用，资源保留必要 HEAD、内容类型和缓存隔离语义。
- 可信 Demo 身份在实际路由提前分流，不读取真实数据库、静态上游、R2或外部资源，不产生写入。过期、混合身份与直接写请求保留原边界。
- 共享预览按模式、语言与演示代际退役旧响应，不能只凭房间代码缓存。现有课堂/考试的未知教室事实保持诚实，普通用户既有预览行为保留。
- 完成双语桌面/手机必要匹配截图、实际 API/图像与禁写/隐私验证、模式切换验证及必要普通回归；独立审查和当前提交 CI 通过后交付。

不启用生产 Demo 开关，不另造地图工作台或修改真实地图资料。

issue.title: feat(demo): browse existing API reference without request execution
issue.body:
Part of #548. Support reading the existing API reference in Demo; do not grant API authority or introduce a separate documentation UI.

## Acceptance

- Reuse `/api/docs`, its existing canonical redirect and `/api/docs/{path}` navigation, localized copy and the existing current OpenAPI document. Keep ordinary documentation and the normative contract unchanged.
- Allow only the exact trusted Demo GET/HEAD/page-data/spec reads required for browsing. Define and verify the actual local-spec delivery policy before implementation: exercise owned ASSETS (or a proven no-binding local source), account explicitly for any permitted local-static binding reads, and prove no external origin, DB/KV/R2 or other business reads. Do not infer zero I/O from the static SSR loader or hide ASSETS calls from observations.
- Guard the actual Scalar reference so Demo cannot authorize, retain real credentials, choose an external server or execute requests, including read requests. Disabling agent/MCP/persisted auth alone is insufficient. No fake principal, SDK authentication bypass or production flag change.
- Keep tag/operation/model reading and navigation usable. Clear retired interactive/auth state across ordinary-to-Demo, locale and exit/re-entry transitions; unknown paths, expired/mixed identities, writes and unrelated API calls remain fail-closed.

## Validation

Independent source and current Scalar-contract review; real owned spec/ASSETS and boundary HTTP controls, request-execution/outbound observations, normal-reader compatibility and same-page lifecycle controls; targeted bilingual desktop/phone reading and native visual evidence. Preserve budgets and original test deadlines. This is the existing readonly requirement, not a new product decision.

issue.title: feat(demo): support existing read-only legal and usage guides
issue.body:
Part of #548. Make existing informational pages usable from the Demo shell without changing their real legal or instructional content.

## Acceptance

- Reuse `/terms`, `/privacy`, `/guides/markdown-support` and `/usage/mobile`, `/usage/bot`, `/usage/cli`, `/usage/mcp` with their existing localized content and local illustrations. Retain `/community/comments/guide` as its existing redirect. Do not fictionalize terms, privacy policy or installation instructions, and do not add a new help/workbench UI.
- Admit only the required GET/HEAD, page-data and exact redirect destinations after trusted Demo identity validation. Preserve the existing MCP client selection query. Writes and unrelated OAuth/admin/settings/upload families remain blocked; normal readers remain unchanged.
- Preserve local reading interactions, language changes and copy-to-clipboard. Real external authorization, installation, download/store and group-join actions stay disabled with an accessible explanation in Demo; do not execute commands or open those flows on behalf of the reader.
- Keep Demo/read-only identity clear without altering the source documents. Guard identity/locale transitions so a retired ordinary document or response does not restore active controls.

## Validation

Independent source review; owned SSR/page-data/HEAD/redirect and invalid-identity controls; precise denied-write checks and no business/external I/O; representative bilingual desktop/phone reading, copy and transition controls with native visual evidence. Keep the production Demo flag unchanged. API reference browsing is a separate leaf.

issue.title: feat(demo): add read-only public author profiles
issue.body:
Part of #548. Extend the existing public profile page and API, separately from the delivered account settings profile.

## Acceptance

- Support the existing `/community/users/{identifier}` and `/api/community/users/{identifier}` for the two established discussion authors: IDs `demo-community-xia` / `demo-community-qiu` and usernames `sample-xia` / `sample-qiu`. Keep their names, local avatars and identity consistent with existing Demo discussions; do not create an authenticated viewer or database user.
- Derive public comment counts and contribution cells from the same closed discussion graph, using the ordinary visibility/deletion/anonymous rules. Use the shared fixed Demo reference date and Sunday-first heatmap. Do not attribute sample homework or uploads to these authors when the source graph has no such authorship, and do not invent upload links.
- Trusted Demo SSR, page-data and API reads return the same fixed profile/counts/heatmap before any real profile reader. Unknown or real identifiers return 404 without DB, KV, R2 or external reads. Expired/mixed identities and writes remain rejected; ordinary profiles remain unchanged.
- Keep the existing profile layout, bilingual labels and readable counts/heatmap. Retire old ordinary/locale responses and identity data when the same page changes mode.

## Validation

Independent source review; pure graph/count/date controls; real owned Worker SSR/API known and foreign positive/negative controls, write rejection and effects/state invariants; targeted identity/locale browser controls and native desktop/phone visual evidence. No production Demo enablement.

issue.title: fix(calendar): unify native calendars on Sunday teaching weeks
issue.body:
## Problem and product decision

The product now requires every calendar to start Sunday, following the university teaching-week calendar. Personal/workspace weeks currently start Monday, public Young weeks/months start Sunday, and legacy timetable/Widget week bounds depend on an implicit Gregorian locale setting. Native date-picker calendar environments are also inconsistent.

Official USTC examples: [2026 autumn calendar](https://www.teach.ustc.edu.cn/calendar/20135.html), week 1 August 30–September 5; [2026 spring calendar](https://www.teach.ustc.edu.cn/calendar/19714.html), week 1 March 1–7. The Sunday decision is explicit; this issue tracks implementation and acceptance, separately from dependency PR #139 and existing native acceptance PR #140.

## Scope

- Use an explicit Foundation Gregorian/Asia-Shanghai/Sunday product calendar shared by the app and Widget without adding Server or LifeClientCore dependencies to the Widget.
- Align personal/workspace/Young week boundaries, legacy timetable, Widget and native date-picker month views. Keep public Sunday grids and shared client-core arbitrary-weekday support.
- For undated server meetings, use Sunday teaching-week bounds with the API weekday mapping Mon1…Sun7. Explicit meeting dates remain authoritative; preserve stored teaching week and rescheduled dates.
- Verify the first official Sunday when raw semester start is later, final-week limits, half-open week/day membership and selected teaching-week labels without rewriting stored class/deadline timestamps.
- Preserve existing owner/session/API-error/request assertions and canonical event identities.

## Acceptance

- Add focused unit regressions for Shanghai Sunday boundaries, all seven weekday offsets, explicit-date precedence, first/last semester weeks, legacy/Widget membership and date-picker policy.
- Update the existing contradictory Monday-first assertions and documentation; preserve generic client-core weekday coverage.
- Independent source review plus current-head original native unit/UI gates, signed App/Widget build and matched iPhone/iPad Chinese/English calendar comparisons. Local Linux checks alone do not establish native acceptance.
- Production OAuth remains separate. Automatic TestFlight is authorized after acceptance; App Store publication still requires explicit confirmation.

issue.title: fix(young): resolve overlapping event-poster and inline-image routes
issue.body:
The Young catalog has two public route patterns that both accept `/api/catalog/young-events/images/image`:

- `/api/catalog/young-events/[youngId]/image` resolves an event poster and returns a no-store 302 to the local immutable image URL.
- `/api/catalog/young-events/images/[...path]` serves an inline image through R2 and its upstream fallback.

An independent read-only audit of the compiled SvelteKit route table found the static `images` namespace is selected first, interpreting `image` as the image path. The existing event-ID schema permits any trimmed nonempty string; Prisma uses a string without a numeric constraint, and repository seed data contains nonnumeric event IDs. Consequently the current contract does not exclude an event whose ID is `images`. This ambiguity predates the Demo work; no production occurrence of that ID has been established.

## Required investigation and acceptance

- Reproduce with an owned database event whose ID is `images`, a safe local poster path, and an owned R2 object. Disable redirect following and prove which handler answers the exact request without contacting the external poster origin.
- Preserve ordinary event-poster lookup and existing immutable inline-image URLs, cache headers and conditional requests. Do not narrow the event-ID schema to numbers or rename public URLs merely to avoid the collision.
- Resolve the route ambiguity and add meaningful real-HTTP regression coverage for the colliding event, ordinary events and immutable images, with isolated cleanup and no external fetch.
- Check trusted Demo image boundaries as well as ordinary requests. Independently review the actual final route table and run relevant validation before merging.

Relevant source: `src/routes/api/catalog/young-events/images/[...path]/+server.ts`, `src/routes/api/catalog/young-events/[youngId]/image/+server.ts`, `src/lib/api/schemas/request-path-schemas.ts`, `src/lib/api/routes/young-event-routes.ts`, and `src/features/young/server/young-event-image-service.ts`.

## Confirmed owned HTTP result and compatible implementation

A fresh main `1fb350a9` Worker reproduced both resources simultaneously in an isolated database/R2 namespace. An ordinary event ID returned the expected no-store 302; its immutable poster returned the exact owned PNG and conditional 304. The colliding `/young-events/images/image` returned the other owned inline PNG with immutable caching and no Location header. The real outbound probe was empty; no upstream poster was fetched. This proves the collision, not a completed fix or a production occurrence.

Changing precedence would reinterpret an already valid immutable URL. The implementation will instead establish `/api/catalog/young-events/by-id/{youngId}/image` as the unambiguous canonical resolver, retain legacy and immutable behavior, and explicitly document the legacy overlap. Its three segments do not collide with the existing two-segment event resolver or the static `images` prefix. Existing Web/GraphQL/CLI/Bot/iOS display code correctly consumes immutable DTO `imageUrl` values and will keep doing so; it has no handwritten legacy resolver call to migrate. The actual by-ID contract is exposed through OpenAPI, generated clients, generic CLI API registration and protocol tests. Server protocol consumers will move to the canonical operation; generated client synchronization follows when that server contract is stable.

Acceptance must prove both the canonical colliding-ID 302 and the unchanged legacy inline 200, plus ordinary/immutable/conditional/HEAD and trusted Demo isolation. Do not report that the old ambiguous URL has become an event redirect. Server implementation is now in PR #1553 (`5e1aeb88526ae2fae6f5d42bca944b7dd65d52fe`), independently reviewed and validated with 191 related units and five real HTTP cases. Both `images` and `by-id` have canonical GET/HEAD redirect controls, while legacy `by-id` still redirects and the old ambiguous inline URI keeps its original bytes/cache. The current-head workflow and all 47 checks passed; PR #1553 is now merged as `735f06b00d0a6067cbcc5fdfd0761103747f8782` with the reviewed tree unchanged. The server canonical resolver is delivered. This issue remains OPEN for main-based generated-client synchronization; existing immutable display URLs are unchanged.


## Generated consumer delivery — complete

Server PR #1553 merged as `735f06b00d0a6067cbcc5fdfd0761103747f8782` after all 47 checks passed. The independently reviewed tree matches the actual merge tree.

Both companions are also merged: [CLI #118](https://github.com/Life-USTC/cli/pull/118) at `d5976621e9da1bb1e20ccae7684dab8f2e4498c8` after 4/4 checks, and [Bot #256](https://github.com/Life-USTC/bot/pull/256) at `3db7b3f9ae03973f88e6beb1248ee7caa907d417` after 6/6 checks. Both merged trees match their reviewed/tested heads. The canonical operation and legacy operation are present in both actual main contracts; the source pin is the real merged server commit and the exact API SHA-256 is `9df7dd68d6b4a62148d8b8f2164a507a613cf353eff65af261cd63a424a32217`. Existing repository provenance verifiers and exact Git blobs were checked, and both local main checkouts are clean and synchronized.

Independent source reviews and clean committed race/semantic validation passed.
